definition_zh: 预测；预言；预报；预料；预示
definition_en: to say or state in advance that something will happen, especially on the basis of evidence or reasoning
core_image: 站在今天，用话把明天的那件事先说出来
scene: 经济学家预测明年的增长会放缓。 Economists predict slower growth next year.
sceneCN: 这里 predict 是「依据数据对将来作出判断」（第 2 个义项：预测）；句意：经济学家预测明年增长会放缓。场景要点：用现有信息、指向未来、可被检验；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 预测；预言
可预测的；意料之中的
预测者；预测指标
不可预测的；变化莫测的

senses.title: To say what will happen
senses.titleCN: 预测：先说将来会发生什么
senses.definition: to state in advance that a particular event will happen
senses.definitionCN: 事先说明某个特定事件将会发生
senses.example: No one could predict which team would win.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人能预测哪支队伍会赢。
senses.why: Latin praedicere is prae 'before' plus dicere 'say'. The plain sense is saying something before it becomes true.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praedicere 是 prae“在前”加 dicere“说”。最朴素的意思，就是在事情成真之前先把它说出来。

senses.title: To forecast from evidence
senses.titleCN: 预测：拿现有信息推算未来
senses.definition: to estimate a future state on the basis of data, models, or reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 依据数据、模型或推理估计未来的状况
senses.example: Economists predict slower growth next year.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家预测明年增长会放缓。
senses.why: The saying is not a guess but a calculation. Evidence is fed in, and the statement about the future comes out.
senses.whyCN: 这话不是猜的，而是算的。把证据喂进去，关于未来的陈述就出来了。

senses.title: Scientific prediction
senses.titleCN: 科学预言：理论先说出可检验的结果
senses.definition: to derive a testable consequence from a scientific theory before it is observed
senses.definitionCN: 在观察之前，从科学理论推出一个可检验的结果
senses.example: The theory predicted a new particle, which was found years later.
senses.exampleCN: 该理论预言了一种新粒子，数年后被找到。
senses.why: A good theory must be able to say what will be seen. Prediction is the test that separates science from speculation.
senses.whyCN: 好的理论必须能说出将会看到什么。预测是把科学与空想分开的那场考试。

senses.title: To indicate in advance by signs
senses.titleCN: 预示：迹象先替将来开口
senses.definition: to be a sign that something will happen, without anyone saying it in words
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事将会发生的迹象，而非由人用话说出
senses.example: Dark clouds predicted a heavy storm.
senses.exampleCN: 乌云预示着大风暴。
senses.why: Signs can speak. When the world itself shows what is coming, we extend the verb from the speaker to the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 迹象也能说话。当世界本身显露出即将发生的事，我们就把这个动词从说话者扩展到证据上。

senses.title: To prophesy
senses.titleCN: 预言：以先知的口吻宣告
senses.definition: to foretell future events as a prophet or oracle does, often without evidence
senses.definitionCN: 像先知或神谕那样预告未来，常无证据支持
senses.example: The old woman predicted that the drought would last seven years.
senses.exampleCN: 老妇人预言旱情会持续七年。
senses.why: The same act of speaking first, but the authority comes from revelation rather than from data.
senses.whyCN: 同样是先说出口的动作，只是权威来自启示而非数据。

senses.title: To expect or anticipate
senses.titleCN: 预料：心里已经先把它算上
senses.definition: to expect something to happen, often in everyday planning
senses.definitionCN: 预期某事会发生，常用于日常安排
senses.example: We predicted heavy traffic and left an hour early.
senses.exampleCN: 我们预料会堵车，所以提前一小时出发。
senses.why: Prediction need not be public. Private anticipation is the same forward-looking move, kept inside the head.
senses.whyCN: 预测不必公开。私下的预料是同一个朝前的动作，只是留在脑子里。

senses.title: Statistics: to estimate a value
senses.definition: to produce an estimated value for a future or unknown observation from a model
senses.definitionCN: 用模型为未来或未知的观测给出一个估计值
senses.example: The model predicts sales of 12,000 units in the first quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 模型预测第一季度销量为一万二千件。
senses.why: In statistics the prediction is a number with an interval, not a sentence. The verb becomes a technical operation.
senses.whyCN: 在统计学里，预测是一个带区间的数，而不是一句话。这个动词变成了一项技术操作。

senses.title: To warn in advance
senses.titleCN: 预告：提前提醒，好让人准备
senses.definition: to announce something in advance so that people can prepare for it
senses.definitionCN: 事先告知某事，以便人们可以准备
senses.example: The report predicted shortages and urged hospitals to stock up.
senses.exampleCN: 报告预告了短缺，并敦促医院囤货。
senses.why: Saying it early has a use: it buys time. Prediction becomes a warning when the future it names is unwelcome.
senses.whyCN: 提前说出来是有用的：它买来时间。当所命名的未来不受欢迎时，预测就成了预警。

intro.en: Predict is a Latin compound meaning to say beforehand. It is one of a large family built on the verb dicere, to say.
intro.cn: predict 是一个意为“事先说出”的拉丁复合词。它属于一个建立在动词 dicere（说）之上的大词族。

items.en: Dicere meant 'to say, declare'. It is the source of diction, dictionary, verdict, contradict, and predict.
items.cn: dicere 意为“说、宣告”。它是 diction、dictionary、verdict、contradict、predict 的来源。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front'. Joined to a verb of saying, it produces the sense of saying something before its time.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前”。与表示“说”的动词结合，就产生“在时间之前说出来”的意思。

items.en: Praedicere meant 'to make known beforehand, to declare in advance'. It was used for foretelling as well as for public proclamation.
items.cn: praedicere 意为“事先让人知道、预先宣告”。它既用于预言，也用于公开宣布。

items.en: The past participle praedictus meant 'foretold'. English keeps it inside words like prediction and predictably.
items.cn: 过去分词 praedictus 意为“被预言的”。英语把它保留在 prediction、predictably 这类词里。

items.en: English predict appears in the 16th century, at first in religious and learned writing about foretelling. The modern data-based sense develops much later.
items.cn: 英语 predict 出现于 16 世纪，最早见于谈论预言的宗教与学术写作。以数据为基础的现代义要晚得多才发展出来。

items.en: With the rise of science and statistics, predict becomes the standard word for evidence-based foretelling, while prophesy remains the religious term.
items.cn: 随着科学与统计的兴起，predict 成了“有据预告”的标准词，而 prophesy 保持宗教色彩。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for saying. The second group collects words for foretelling, each with a different basis of authority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“说”的动词。第二组收表示“预告”的词，各自依据的权威不同。

entries.definition: a statement about what will happen. It is the noun built on predict with -ion.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将会发生什么的陈述。它是 predict 加 -ion 构成的名词。

entries.definition: able to be foreseen, often with a hint of dullness. Predict plus -able.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被预见的，常带一点乏味的暗示。predict 加 -able。

entries.definition: the part of a sentence that says something about the subject, or to base something on. It comes from Latin praedicare, a cousin of praedicere.
entries.definitionCN: 句子中陈述主语的部分，或“以……为依据”。它来自拉丁 praedicare，是 praedicere 的近亲。

entries.definition: a decision or judgement. Ver- 'true' plus dict 'said': what is said as true.
entries.definitionCN: 裁决或判定。ver-“真”加 dict“说”：被说成真实的话。

entries.definition: to say what is likely in weather, economics, or other systems. Forecast is common for weather and trends; predict is the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 预告天气、经济或其他系统的可能状况。forecast 多用于天气与趋势；predict 是一般用语。

entries.definition: to tell of a future event. Foretell is literary and often implies a sign or a seer.
entries.definitionCN: 讲述未来的事件。foretell 带文学色彩，常暗示有征兆或预言者。

entries.definition: to foretell under divine inspiration. Prophesy claims a religious authority that predict does not.
entries.definitionCN: 在神圣启示下预告未来。prophesy 主张一种宗教权威，predict 没有这种主张。

entries.definition: to expect something and often act in advance. Anticipate adds preparation; predict can be purely a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 预期某事并常提前行动。anticipate 多出“准备”之意；predict 可以只是陈述。

entries.definition: to estimate future figures from present trends. Project is technical and numerical, closer to sense 07.
entries.definitionCN: 由当前趋势估算未来数字。project 是技术性、数值性的，更接近第 7 义项。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the sentence said too early, the economist's model, the particle found later, the dark clouds, and the shopping list made before the rush.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：提早说出的那句话、经济学家的模型、后来找到的粒子、乌云、以及抢购前先列好的清单。

normal.en: Pre- means before, dict means say. Predict is say-before.
normal.cn: pre- 是“在前”，dict 是“说”。predict 就是“先说”。

normal.en: A weather forecast and a stock forecast are both predict with numbers plugged in.
normal.cn: 天气预报和股市预测，都是把数字代进去的 predict。

normal.en: A theory predicts a particle, then the lab goes looking for it. Prediction is the theory's exam.
normal.cn: 理论预言一种粒子，实验室随后去找它。预测就是理论的那场考试。

normal.en: Dark clouds predict rain without saying a word: signs can also speak.
normal.cn: 乌云一言不发就预示下雨：迹象也会说话。

normal.en: Predicting a rush and leaving early is the same verb, just kept private.
normal.cn: 预料拥堵并提早出门，是同一个动词，只是留在心里。

abstract.en: Every prediction is a promise the present makes about the future, and it can be broken by a single unforeseen event.
abstract.cn: 每个预测都是现在对未来作出的承诺，而它可能被一个未预见的事件打破。

abstract.en: The difference between prophecy and prediction is not the content but the warrant: revelation versus evidence.
abstract.cn: 预言与预测的差别不在内容，而在凭据：是启示，还是证据。

abstract.en: To predict well is to be willing to be wrong in public, which is why science prizes it.
abstract.cn: 预测得好，意味着愿意在公众面前出错；正因如此，科学看重它。

examples.en: The model predicts that sea levels will rise by about half a metre this century.
examples.cn: 该模型预测本世纪海平面将上升约半米。

examples.en: As predicted, the first frost came in the last week of October.
examples.cn: 正如所料，初霜在十月最后一周到来。

examples.en: Analysts predict a sharp fall in demand for new cars.
examples.cn: 分析人士预测新车需求将大幅下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞迪克特”——普瑞提前把“迪克特”那件事说出口，就是 predict（预测）

root: 拉丁语 praedicere“事先说出、预先宣告”＝prae“在前”+ dicere“说” → 英语 predict（16 世纪）；与 diction、dictionary、verdict、contradict 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The word always means saying something before it happens. What changes is the basis: evidence, theory, signs, revelation, private expectation, or a statistical model. Each basis gives a slightly different shade of the same forward-speaking act.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终指“在事情发生之前先说出来”。变化的是依据：证据、理论、征兆、启示、私下预期，或统计模型。每一种依据都给同一个“朝前说话”的动作一种不同的色调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence spoken today about an event that has not yet arrived.
core.cn: 核心意象：今天说出一句话，说的是尚未到来的事件。

branches.en: SPEECH: saying or expecting, public or private.
branches.cn: 言语：说出或预料，公开或私下。

branches.en: CALCULATION: forecasts from data, and statistical estimates.
branches.cn: 计算：由数据作出的预报，以及统计估计。

branches.en: SCIENCE: the theory that names a result before it is observed.
branches.cn: 科学：在结果被观察之前就把它命名的理论。

branches.en: SIGN AND WARNING: the world speaking through evidence, and the early notice that buys time.
branches.cn: 征兆与预警：世界借证据说话，以及买来时间的提前告知。

branches.en: PROPHECY: the same act, warranted by revelation.
branches.cn: 预言：同一个动作，凭据是启示。

intro.en: Predict is one compound from the large dicere family. Every word below is either a piece of that compound or a sibling built with another prefix on the same verb of saying.
intro.cn: predict 是 dicere 大词族里的一个复合词。下面每个词，要么是这个复合词的构件，要么是在同一个“说”的动词上加别的前缀构成的兄弟词。

latinIntro.en: Latin praedicere and its participle praedictus supplied the English forms; the same dic- stem appears across law, grammar, and everyday speech.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praedicere 及其分词 praedictus 提供了英语形式；同一个 dic- 词干出现在法律、语法与日常言语中。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀

definition_zh: 课；课程；教训；一堂课的时间
definition_en: a period of teaching; a piece of content studied; an experience that teaches you something
core_image: 黑板前的一段时间，离开时你比来时知道得多
scene: 雨天的午后，音乐教室里传来断续的琴声。 The first lesson begins at eight sharp.
sceneCN: 这里 lesson 是「教学时段」（第 1 个义项：一节课）；句意为第一节课八点整开始。

pos.zh: 课程内容；功课外的东西

derivatives.zh: lesson 加 -ing 名词化，指「授课过程」（罕用）
加否定前缀 un-，指「未受过教的」（罕用）

senses.title: A period of teaching
senses.definition: a set period in which someone is taught
senses.definitionCN: 安排好的教学时段
senses.example: The first lesson begins at eight sharp.
senses.exampleCN: 第一节课八点整开始。
senses.why: The reading is part of lesson: a portion read aloud became a portion taught.
senses.whyCN: 「诵读的部分」是 lesson 的本义：读的一段变成了教的一段。

senses.title: The content studied
senses.definition: the material or subject covered in teaching
senses.definitionCN: 教学中涵盖的材料或科目
senses.example: Today\u2019s lesson is about rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 今天的课讲河流。
senses.why: The period and what fills it share the name, since the lesson is what is delivered.
senses.whyCN: 时段与其中所授共享其名，因为 lesson 就是所授之物。

senses.title: An experience that teaches
senses.definition: something learned from experience, often a hard one
senses.definitionCN: 从经历中学到的东西，常含挫折
senses.example: The accident taught him a lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 那次事故给了他一个教训。
senses.why: Life also delivers portions of instruction, so the classroom word covers the school of hard knocks.
senses.whyCN: 生活也会「授课」，课堂之词于是覆盖了社会这所学校。

senses.title: A passage from scripture
senses.definition: a passage read aloud in church services
senses.definitionCN: 礼拜中朗读的经文段落
senses.example: The second lesson comes from the gospel.
senses.exampleCN: 第二段诵读取自福音书。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense kept: the reading portion survives in church use.
senses.whyCN: 这是保存最久的义项：诵读段落留存于教会用法。

senses.title: A warning meant to correct
senses.definition: a punishment or rebuke intended to teach someone better
senses.definitionCN: 意在使人改正的惩罚或训诫
senses.example: The coach gave them a hard lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 教练狠狠敲打了他们一顿。
senses.why: A sharp correction is a lesson in disguise, delivered without a classroom.
senses.whyCN: 严厉的纠正是伪装的课，只是不在教室里上。

senses.title: A unit in a course or book
senses.definition: a numbered unit of a course or textbook
senses.definitionCN: 课程或教材中编号的一单元
senses.example: Unit five has ten lessons.
senses.exampleCN: 第五单元有十课。
senses.why: Books slice teaching into portions, each portion keeping the old word.
senses.whyCN: 书籍把教学切成段落，每段沿用旧词。

intro.en: Lesson comes from Old French lecon, from Medieval Latin lecio, from Latin lectio "a reading", built on legere "to read, gather".
intro.cn: lesson 来自古法语 lecon，出自中世纪拉丁语 lecio，再溯至拉丁语 lectio「诵读」，建立在 legere「读、采集」之上。

items.en: Latin legere meant 'to gather, read', the same root as legible and lectern.
items.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为「采集、读」，与 legible、lectern 同根。

items.en: Latin lectio meant 'a reading', especially a passage read aloud, as in church.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lectio 意为「诵读」，尤指朗读的段落，见于教会。

items.en: Medieval Latin lecio shifted to mean a piece of teaching itself.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 lecio 转指教学本身的一部分。

items.en: Old French lecon carried the teaching sense into English spelling and sound.
items.cn: 古法语 lecon 把教学义带入英语的拼写与读音。

items.en: Modern English spread lesson to classes, books, punishments and the school of experience.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lesson 扩展到课堂、教材、惩戒与经验之校。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes; group two collects teaching words.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近词；第二组收集教学之词。

entries.definition: The verb to reduce; identical in sound, unrelated in root.
entries.definitionCN: 减少的动词；同音但词根无关。

entries.definition: The comparative amount word; shares letters only.
entries.definitionCN: 比较级「更少」；只是字母相叠。

entries.definition: From the same Latin legere family; a long talk of teaching.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁 legere 词族；指较长的授课演讲。

entries.definition: The group or session; lesson stresses the content taught.
entries.definitionCN: 班级或课时；lesson 强调所授内容。

entries.definition: Teaching, often step by step; more formal than lesson.
entries.definitionCN: 教学，多为分步；比 lesson 正式。

entries.definition: The lesson drawn from a story, especially a fable.
entries.definitionCN: 从故事中得出的寓意，尤指寓言。

entries.definition: A period of activity or study; broader than a lesson.
entries.definitionCN: 活动或学习的一段；比 lesson 更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin root and real phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁词根与真实短语。

normal.en: Latin lectio meant a reading; a lesson began as a read portion.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lectio 意为诵读；lesson 起初就是读的一段。

normal.en: The same root gives lecture, legible and lectern.
normal.cn: 同根词有 lecture、legible、lectern。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: give a lesson, learn a lesson, teach someone a lesson.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：授课、吸取教训、教训某人。

normal.en: Churches still call scripture readings the lessons.
normal.cn: 教会至今把诵读经文叫 lessons。

normal.en: A lesson plan is the teacher\u2019s map for one class.
normal.cn: 教案是教师一节课的路线图。

abstract.en: Picture a bell, and forty heads bending over one page.
abstract.cn: 想象铃声响后，四十个脑袋凑向同一页。

abstract.en: Picture a bruise that remembers the warning better than words.
abstract.cn: 想象一块淤青比言语更牢地记住警告。

abstract.en: Picture a pulpit light on one open scripture page.
abstract.cn: 想象讲坛灯光落在一页摊开的经文上。

examples.en: Piano lessons cost twice as much this year.
examples.cn: 今年钢琴课涨了一倍。

examples.en: Every failure carries a lesson if you look for it.
examples.cn: 只要去找，每次失败都藏着一课。

examples.en: The vicar read the first lesson from Isaiah.
examples.cn: 牧师领读了取自以赛亚书的第一段经文。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「雷声」——老师讲课时如雷贯耳 → 课；教训

root: 拉丁语 lectio「诵读」（legere「读、采集」）→ 中世纪拉丁语 lecio → 古法语 lecon → 英语 lesson；与 lecture 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses all keep the shape of a portion delivered: a reading, a class, its content, a unit, a warning, and a hard-won truth.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都保留「被交付的一段」的形状：诵读、课、内容、单元、警告与苦得的道理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a measured portion of teaching, handed over like a read passage.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段有定量的教学，如诵读般交付。

branches.en: MEASURED TIME: the class period and the book unit.
branches.cn: 定量时间：课堂时段与教材单元。

branches.en: WHAT IS DELIVERED: the content inside the period.
branches.cn: 所授之物：时段里的内容。

branches.en: THE OLDEST SENSE: scripture readings survive in church.
branches.cn: 最老义项：教会里存活的经文诵读。

branches.en: THE HARD SCHOOL: experience and punishment both teach.
branches.cn: 严苛学校：经验与惩戒皆可施教。

branches.en: THE PIVOT: every sense is a portion handed over.
branches.cn: 轴心：每个义项都是交付的一段。

intro.en: Lesson is a borrowed noun with no English affixes of its own; derivatives are rare and attach native prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: lesson 是无本族词缀的外来名词；派生词少见，附加本族前后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root legere gives cousins like lecture, so the Latin section lists them; no direct Latin cognate of lesson itself is listed separately.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 legere 提供 lecture 等同族词，拉丁部分列出它们；lesson 本体的直接拉丁同源词不另列。

items.example: A cousin from the same root.

derivatives.zh: 授课（罕用）
未受教的（罕用）

definition_zh: 服装；衣物（总称）
definition_en: garments in general; the things people wear considered as one group
core_image: 把所有人的衣裳装进一个大箱子，统称服装
scene: 冬季运动会前，体育老师提醒大家多带衣物。 Warm clothing is needed for the winter camp.
sceneCN: 这里 clothing 是「服装（总称）」（第 1 个义项：衣服的整体概念，不可数）；句意是冬令营需要带保暖衣物。

derivatives.zh: 由 cloth 加 -e 构成，义为「给…穿衣」
与 clothing 同源，义为「衣服（复数形式）」

senses.title: Garments considered as a whole
senses.definition: all the garments people wear, treated as one uncountable group
senses.definitionCN: 人们穿的衣物被当作一个整体
senses.example: The shop sells sports clothing for children.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店卖儿童运动服装。
senses.why: Many separate shirts and coats can be gathered into one big idea, like water gathered into one river.
senses.whyCN: 一件件衬衫和大衣可以汇成一个整体概念，就像水汇成一条河。

senses.title: A covering that protects the body
senses.definition: a layer that covers and protects the body
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖并保护身体的层
senses.example: Firefighters wear special protective clothing.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员穿特殊的防护服。
senses.why: When cloth is worn for safety rather than style, the general word for garments still fits.
senses.whyCN: 当衣物是为了安全而非美观时，衣物的总称词依然适用。

intro.en: Clothing is cloth put to work, with a very old ending doing the job.
intro.cn: clothing 是被派上用场的 cloth，由一个古老的词缀来担当。

items.en: The base *klotham gave Old English clath, the bare word for cloth.
items.cn: 词基 *klotham 给了古英语 clath，即布的本词。

items.en: Old English already used clathing for garments as a whole.
items.cn: 古英语已用 clathing 指衣物的整体。

items.en: Middle English spelling varied, and the -ing form slowly won out.
items.cn: 中古英语拼法多样，-ing 形式逐渐胜出。

items.en: Modern English fixed clothing as the formal, uncountable word for garments.
items.cn: 现代英语把 clothing 定为不可数的正式说法。

items.en: Today clothing competes with clothes: clothes is casual, clothing is for shops and signs.
items.cn: 如今 clothing 与 clothes 并存：clothes 偏口语，clothing 用于店名与标签。

note.en: The first group collects the cloth family; the second collects garment words.
note.cn: 第一组收 cloth 词族，第二组收服装类词。

entries.definition: The things you wear, everyday plural.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衣服」，与 clothing 同源，更口语。

entries.definition: Woven material.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「布料」，是词族的源头。

entries.definition: The act of coming to an end.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结束」，拼写与 clothing 相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: One single piece of clothing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一件衣服」，可数。

entries.definition: Clothing, in formal or commercial style.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「服装」，正式或商业用语。

entries.definition: A suffix-like word for clothing types, as in footwear.
entries.definitionCN: 常作复合词后缀，如 footwear「鞋类」。

normalIntro.en: Remember clothing as the whole box of garments.
normalIntro.cn: 把 clothing 记成一整箱衣裳。

normal.en: clothing is uncountable: no clothing-s.
normal.cn: clothing 不可数，没有复数。

normal.en: one shirt is a piece of clothing.
normal.cn: 一件衬衫是 a piece of clothing。

normal.en: clothing sounds formal, clothes sounds casual.
normal.cn: clothing 偏正式，clothes 偏口语。

normal.en: protective clothing keeps workers safe.
normal.cn: protective clothing 保护工人安全。

normal.en: clothing comes from cloth plus -ing.
normal.cn: clothing 由 cloth 加 -ing 构成。

abstract.en: See one giant drawer holding every coat you own.
abstract.cn: 想象一个巨大抽屉装下你所有的大衣。

abstract.en: Feel a raincoat snap shut against the storm.
abstract.cn: 感受雨衣在风雨中扣紧。

abstract.en: Hear the hanger rack slide along in a big shop.
abstract.cn: 听大卖场里挂衣杆滑动的声音。

examples.en: Bring enough clothing for the five-day trip.
examples.cn: 为五天的旅行带够衣物。

examples.en: The old clothing was collected for recycling.
examples.cn: 旧衣物被集中回收。

examples.en: Lab workers must wear protective clothing.
examples.cn: 实验室人员必须穿防护服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克洛星」——衣服多得像星星挂满衣柜，clothing 就是满天星星般的衣物总称。

root: 日耳曼语 *klotham → 古英语 clath（布）→ clathing（衣物总称）→ 中古英语 → 现代英语 clothing；同源词有 cloth（布）、clothes（衣服）、clothe（穿衣）。

sensesIntro.en: Clothing gathers garments into one whole and can also mean protective coverings.
sensesIntro.cn: clothing 把衣物汇成整体，也可指起保护作用的覆盖物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: all garments gathered into one big whole
core.cn: 核心意象：所有衣裳汇成的一个整体

branches.en: Garments as one group
branches.cn: 作为整体的衣物

branches.en: Protective layers
branches.cn: 保护性覆盖

branches.en: Shops and labels
branches.cn: 商店与标签用语

branches.en: Cotton, wool and silk made wearable
branches.cn: 可穿的棉毛丝

branches.en: Cloth in daily service
branches.cn: 布料的日常用途

intro.en: The -ing ending turns a small noun into a big collective idea.
intro.cn: -ing 词缀把小名词变成大的集合概念。

latinIntro.en: Clothing is Germanic, so Latin relatives are absent from this family.
latinIntro.cn: clothing 属日耳曼词源，家族中没有拉丁亲戚。

items.example: The program clothes hundreds of children.
items.exampleCN: 该项目为数百名儿童提供衣物。

items.example: Wrap the bowl in a cloth.
The garment is made of silk.

definition_zh: 决心；决议；解决；分辨率
definition_en: a firm decision, a formal vote, the solving of a problem, or image sharpness
core_image: 一个人把复杂纠缠的线团一点点解开，最后拉直
scene: 新年第一天，她下定决心每天早起读书。 On the first day of the new year, she made a resolution to read every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 resolution 是「决心」（第 1 个义项：坚定的决定）；句意：新年第一天，她下定决心每天早起读书。

derivatives.zh: 解决；决心
下定决心的
坚决的；果断的

senses.title: A firm personal decision
senses.definition: a serious decision to do or stop doing something
senses.definitionCN: 认真决定去做或停止做某事
senses.example: She made a resolution to read every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她下定决心每天早晨读书。
senses.why: The word names the mind settling on a course, like a knot finally pulled straight.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指心思终于定下方向，就像绳结最终被拉直。

senses.title: A formal decision by vote
senses.definition: a formal statement or decision agreed by a group or council
senses.definitionCN: 由团体或委员会表决同意的正式声明或决定
senses.example: The council passed a resolution against the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会通过了一项反对该计划的决议。
senses.why: A group can settle its will as firmly as a person does.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体也能像个人一样坚定地定下意志。

senses.title: The solving of a problem
senses.definition: the act of finding an answer to a difficulty or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 为困难或争端找到答案的行为
senses.example: The resolution of the dispute took months.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争端的解决花了几个月。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to loosen, and solving a problem is loosening it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为松开，而解决问题就是把问题松开。

senses.title: Image sharpness
senses.definition: the amount of detail a screen, image, or lens can show
senses.definitionCN: 屏幕、图像或镜头能显示的细节数量
senses.example: The photograph has very high resolution.
senses.exampleCN: 这张照片的分辨率很高。
senses.why: A high-resolution image can be resolved, or separated, into fine points of detail.
senses.whyCN: 高分辨率图像能被「解析」成细小的细节点。

intro.en: Resolution comes from Latin resolutio, a loosening, from resolvere, to loosen completely, built on re- and solvere.
intro.cn: resolution 来自拉丁语 resolutio（松开），源于 resolvere（彻底解开），由 re- 与 solvere 构成。

items.en: Solvere means to loosen, release, or pay.
items.cn: solvere 意为松开、释放或偿付。

items.en: Resolvere means to loosen completely or dissolve.
items.cn: resolvere 意为彻底解开或溶解。

items.en: Resolutio means a loosening or a settling.
items.cn: resolutio 意为松开、定解。

items.en: Resolution keeps the sense of a firm settling.
items.cn: resolution 保留「坚定定下」的含义。

items.en: Middle English resolution covers decisions and solutions.
items.cn: 中古英语 resolution 兼指决定与解决。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of screen and image sharpness.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了屏幕与图像分辨率的义项。

note.en: Resolution is the noun of resolve, and it sits near its family and near words for decision and solution.
note.cn: resolution 是 resolve 的名词，与自身词族以及表示决定和解决的词相邻。

entries.definition: to solve a problem or decide firmly
entries.definitionCN: 解决；决心

entries.definition: firmly decided
entries.definitionCN: 下定决心的

entries.definition: firm and determined
entries.definitionCN: 坚决的；果断的

entries.definition: a choice that has been made
entries.definitionCN: 决定

entries.definition: an answer to a problem
entries.definitionCN: 解决办法

entries.definition: firmness of purpose
entries.definitionCN: 决心；毅力

normalIntro.en: Resolution is resolve plus -ion: the act of loosening a problem or fixing a decision.
normalIntro.cn: resolution 是 resolve 加 -ion：解开问题或定下决心的行为。

normal.en: Re- means back, and solvere means loosen.
normal.cn: re- 表示回，solvere 表示松开。

normal.en: A New Year's resolution is a promise to yourself.
normal.cn: New Year's resolution 是对自己的承诺。

normal.en: A council resolution is a formal vote.
normal.cn: council resolution 是正式表决。

normal.en: The resolution of a problem is its solution.
normal.cn: 问题的 resolution 就是它的解决办法。

normal.en: High resolution means the image can be resolved into fine detail.
normal.cn: 高分辨率意味着图像能被解析出细腻细节。

abstract.en: Picture a tangled cord straightened strand by strand.
abstract.cn: 想象一团乱绳被一缕缕理直。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand pressing a stamp on a formal paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在正式文件上盖章。

abstract.en: Think of a blurred photo sharpening into clear faces.
abstract.cn: 想象一张模糊照片渐渐显出清晰的面孔。

examples.en: She made a resolution to read every morning.
examples.cn: 她下定决心每天早晨读书。

examples.en: The council passed a resolution against the plan.
examples.cn: 委员会通过了一项反对该计划的决议。

examples.en: The resolution of the dispute took months.
examples.cn: 这场争端的解决花了几个月。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「resolve + ion」——把问题解开、把决心定下，就是 resolution；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 solvere（松开）→ resolvere（彻底解开）→ resolutio（松开、定解）→ 古法语 resolution → 现代英语 resolution。

sensesIntro.en: The noun moves from loosening a problem to settling a decision, then to a formal group vote, and finally to an image resolved into fine detail.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从「解开问题」到「定下决定」，再到群体正式表决，最后指图像被解析出的清晰细节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tangled problem loosened until it lies straight.
core.cn: 核心意象：纠缠的问题被解开，直到平直。

branches.en: A personal decision is the mind settling on one course.
branches.cn: 个人决心，是心思定在一条路上。

branches.en: A formal vote settles a group's will.
branches.cn: 正式表决定下群体的意志。

branches.en: Solving a problem loosens its difficulties.
branches.cn: 解决问题就是把难处解开。

branches.en: Image sharpness separates a picture into fine points.
branches.cn: 图像分辨率把画面分成细小的点。

branches.en: Both a solution and a sharp image depend on separating detail clearly.
branches.cn: 解决办法与清晰图像都依赖把细节分清楚。

intro.en: Resolution is an English -ion noun built on the Latin verb resolvere.
intro.cn: resolution 是建立在拉丁动词 resolvere 上的英语 -ion 名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere means to loosen, and resolvere means to loosen completely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 solvere 意为松开，resolvere 意为彻底解开。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of loosening back.
items.exampleCN: re- 增添「往回松开」的意思。

items.example: Resolvere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: resolvere 把前缀与词根结合。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾

definition_zh: 大学；综合性大学；大学校园
definition_en: a large school for higher education where students study for degrees and research is done
core_image: 一片古老的院落里，几栋教学楼、图书馆与宿舍围成一圈，学生抱着书穿过草坪
scene: 九月清晨，新生拖着箱子在门口停下，抬头看着门楣上刻着校名的石碑。 She chose this university because of its astronomy department.
sceneCN: 这里 university 是「大学」（第 1 个义项：授予学位并进行研究的高等学校）；句意为她因为天文系而选择了这所大学。门口刻着校名的那片院落，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 大学全体师生（集合用法）

derivatives.zh: 与本词同源，义为「普遍的；全体的」
与本词同源，义为「宇宙；全体」
由本词加 -arian 构成，义为「大学的；大学成员的」
由 inter- 加本词构成，义为「校际的」

senses.title: A place that grants degrees
senses.definition: an institution for higher education that awards degrees and carries out research
senses.definitionCN: 授予学位并进行研究的高等教育机构
senses.example: She teaches chemistry at a university in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她在北方的一所大学教化学。
senses.why: Universitas first meant any whole body of people; the guild of teachers and students became this kind of school.
senses.whyCN: universitas 最初指任何一个人的整体；教师与学生的行会后来成了这种学校。

senses.title: The buildings and grounds
senses.definition: the buildings and grounds of such an institution, taken as a place
senses.definitionCN: 这样一所机构的建筑与场地，被当作一个地方
senses.example: The whole university was quiet during the summer holidays.
senses.exampleCN: 暑假期间整个校园都很安静。
senses.why: The abstract body of scholars became a physical place on a map.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的学者团体变成了地图上一个实在的地方。

senses.title: Its members together
senses.definition: all the students and teachers of the institution as a single community
senses.definitionCN: 把一所院校的学生与教师视为一个共同体
senses.example: The university voted to change the name of its main hall.
senses.exampleCN: 全校投票决定更改主楼的名字。
senses.why: The oldest sense survives: a university is still a group of people, not only walls.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意义仍在：大学仍然是一群人，而不只是墙。

senses.title: The idea of higher learning
senses.definition: used generally of higher education as a stage of life or a system
senses.definitionCN: 泛指高等教育这一阶段或这一体系
senses.example: Going to university changes how a young person reads the world.
senses.exampleCN: 上大学会改变一个年轻人看世界的方式。
senses.why: British usage leaves out the article to name the stage itself rather than a building.
senses.whyCN: 英式用法省略冠词，指的是这个阶段本身而不是一栋建筑。

senses.title: Life as a school
senses.definition: in fixed phrases such as the university of life, experience treated as an education
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the university of life 等固定说法，把经历当作一种教育
senses.example: He never finished school, but the university of life taught him plenty.
senses.exampleCN: 他没有念完书，但社会这所大学教了他很多。
senses.why: The word becomes a metaphor: anything that teaches at length is granted its name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词成了比喻：凡是长期教人的东西都被赋予它的名字。

intro.en: University began as a Latin word for any whole body of people, and narrowed to the guild of scholars.
intro.cn: university 起初是拉丁语里指任何人的整体的词，后来收窄为学者的行会。

items.en: Universus meant turned into one, whole, and universitas meant the whole of a group.
items.cn: 拉丁语 universus 意为「合成一个的、整个的」，universitas 意为「一个团体的全体」。

items.en: In the Middle Ages universitas was used for any guild or corporation, including that of teachers and students.
items.cn: 中世纪时 universitas 可指任何行会或法人团体，也包括教师与学生的行会。

items.en: French université was applied specifically to the scholars' guild and the school it ran.
items.cn: 法语 université 专门用来指学者的行会及其所办的学校。

items.en: English took university in the fourteenth century for a school of higher learning with its own rules.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪以 university 指有自身规章的高等学校。

items.en: The word spread with modern degree systems, and British usage dropped the article in go to university.
items.cn: 随着现代学位制度普及，这个词流传开来，英式用法在 go to university 中省略了冠词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same whole-body root; the near-meaning group gathers names for institutions of learning.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「整体」词根上的词；近义组收各类教育机构的名称。

entries.definition: The adjective for what applies to all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「普遍的」。

entries.definition: All of space and matter; the root word of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宇宙」，是这一词族的根词。

entries.definition: The quality of holding for everyone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「普遍性」。

entries.definition: The plural, used for several institutions.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指多所大学。

entries.definition: Variety and difference; close in sound but built on another root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性」，读音相近但词根不同。

entries.definition: A smaller institution or a part of a university; often grants diplomas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院」，规模较小或是大学的一部分。

entries.definition: A school for a special field, or a learned society.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「专科院校、学会」，多用于特定领域。

entries.definition: An organization for research or teaching in one field.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院、研究所」，多指某一领域的研究或教学机构。

entries.definition: A school for technical and applied subjects; in Britain often now a university.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「理工学院」，在英国如今多已成为大学。

entries.definition: A general word for any place of teaching, including primary ones.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学校」，泛指任何教学场所，包括小学。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the old sense of a whole body of people and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词「一群人的整体」的古老意义，以及它常见的搭配。

normal.en: Universitas meant any whole guild: a university is still a whole body of teachers and students.
normal.cn: universitas 指任何完整的行会：大学仍是教师与学生的整体。

normal.en: In British English people say go to university with no article.
normal.cn: 英式英语说 go to university，不加冠词。

normal.en: University student, university degree, university entrance: the word mainly works as an attributive.
normal.cn: university student、university degree、university entrance：这个词多作定语。

normal.en: The plural is universities, with the y turned to ie.
normal.cn: 复数是 universities，y 变为 ie。

normal.en: The university of life is a school without walls.
normal.cn: the university of life 是一所没有围墙的学校。

abstract.en: Picture a gate carved with a name: everyone who walks through becomes part of one body.
abstract.cn: 想象镌刻着校名的大门：走进来的人都成为一个整体的一部分。

abstract.en: The building and the community share one word, because the oldest sense is the people, not the stones.
abstract.cn: 建筑与共同体共用同一个词，因为最古老的意义是人而不是石头。

abstract.en: A university is a place that keeps knowledge alive by passing it on.
abstract.cn: 大学是一个靠传递而让知识活下来的地方。

examples.en: He studied law at a university in Beijing.
examples.cn: 他在北京的一所大学读法律。

examples.en: Most students live on campus during their first year at university.
examples.cn: 多数学生上大学的头一年住在校内。

examples.en: The university has three libraries and a small museum.
examples.cn: 这所大学有三个图书馆和一座小博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼沃西提」——优尼沃西一提校名，人人都成了整体：大学

root: 源自拉丁语 universus「合成一个的、整个的」所生的 universitas「团体的全体」，中世纪指任何行会，包括师生行会；经古法语 université 进入英语，专指有自身规章的高等学校。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of university all rest on one old idea: a whole body of people. That body became a school, then a place, then a stage of life, then a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: university 的五个义项都立在一个古老观念上：一群人的整体。这个整体成了学校，又成了地方、人生阶段，最后成了比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of old buildings around a lawn, with a carved name above the gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片古老建筑围着草坪，门楣上刻着校名。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: the guild became an institution that grants degrees.
branches.cn: 学校线：行会变成了授予学位的机构。

branches.en: THE PLACE: the institution has walls, lawns and libraries.
branches.cn: 地点线：这所机构有墙、草坪与图书馆。

branches.en: THE MEMBERS: the oldest sense, all its students and teachers together.
branches.cn: 成员线：最古老的意义，全体师生合在一起。

branches.en: THE STAGE: going to university names a period of life.
branches.cn: 阶段线：上大学指的是人生的一段时期。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: any long teacher is granted the name.
branches.cn: 比喻线：任何长期的教导者都被赋予这个名字。

intro.en: University is a Latin compound with the Latin suffix -tas, which becomes -ty in English.
intro.cn: university 是带拉丁语后缀 -tas 的复合词，该后缀在英语中变为 -ty。

latinIntro.en: Universus and universitas are both recorded, and the suffix -tas is the standard Latin way to make a noun of quality.
latinIntro.cn: universus 与 universitas 均有记录，-tas 是拉丁语构成性质名词的标准后缀。

items.example: The prefix gathers the group into one.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把人群收成一个。

items.example: The root gives the turning to one side.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出朝向一边转的意思。
它把 universitas 变成 university。

items.meaning: the whole of a body, a guild

items.example: The sense that produced the school.
items.exampleCN: 生出了这种学校的那个义项。

latinEntries.meaning: the whole of a body, a guild

definition_zh: 几乎不；简直不；刚刚才
definition_en: almost not; only just; certainly not
core_image: 门缝里漏进的一线光：光照了，但少得几乎看不见
scene: 考完试他累得说不出一句完整的话，回答时几乎不抬眼皮。 He was so tired after the exam that he hardly spoke during dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 hardly 是「几乎不」（第 1 个义项：程度极低近乎否定）；晚饭时他累得几乎不开口，hardly 把动词说话的意义压到几乎为零。

derivatives.zh: 硬的；困难的，hardly 的基础词，语义本为坚硬或困难
硬度；坚硬，同根名词，指坚硬的性质
耐寒的；强壮的，同根形容词，指能吃苦耐寒

senses.title: Almost not
senses.definition: almost not at all; only a very small amount
senses.definitionCN: 几乎完全不；程度极小
senses.example: There was hardly any food left in the fridge.
senses.exampleCN: 冰箱里几乎没剩下什么食物。
senses.why: Hard originally means with force, and pressing an action down to almost nothing flips the sense into near negation.
senses.whyCN: hard 本义与「用力」相关，把一个动作压到几乎为零，语义便翻转成近乎否定的「几乎不」。

senses.title: Only just
senses.definition: only just; not more than
senses.definitionCN: 仅仅；不超过
senses.example: She had hardly sat down when the phone rang.
senses.exampleCN: 她刚坐下电话就响了。
senses.why: When almost nothing of an action is complete, the time line shows the event barely finished, giving the sense of barely or only just.
senses.whyCN: 当一个动作只完成了一丁点，时间线上就呈现出「勉强完成」，于是有了「刚刚才」的时间义。

intro.en: Hardly grew from the adverbial use of hard and then flipped its meaning.
intro.cn: hardly 由 hard 的副词用法长出，后来语义发生翻转。

items.en: The adjective hard took the adverb suffix -lice to form heardlice, meaning in a hard manner or severely.
items.cn: 古英语形容词 hard 加副词后缀 -lice 构成 heardlice，意为「以强硬的方式、严厉地」。

items.en: In Middle English, hardly still meant boldly or with force, close to the modern word hardly at all.
items.cn: 中古英语里 hardly 仍表示「大胆地、用力地」，与今天的意思相去甚远。

items.en: By the fifteenth century the sense weakened, and hardly came to mean barely or almost not.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，词义弱化，hardly 逐渐表示「勉强地、几乎不」。

items.en: Modern grammars treat hardly as a negative adverb, pairing it with any instead of some.
items.cn: 现代语法把 hardly 视为否定副词，句中要配 any 而不是 some。

items.en: The phrase hardly ever fixed itself as the standard way to say almost never.
items.cn: 短语 hardly ever 固定下来，成为表示「几乎从不」的标准说法。

note.en: Look-alikes and meaning neighbours of hardly.
note.cn: hardly 的形近词与义近词。

entries.definition: firm; difficult; with effort
entries.definitionCN: 硬的；困难的；努力地，同根基础词

entries.definition: severe suffering
entries.definitionCN: 艰难；困苦，同根名词

entries.definition: strong and able to endure
entries.definitionCN: 耐寒的；强壮的，同根形容词，拼写相近

entries.definition: only just; almost not
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅；几乎不，义场几乎重合

entries.definition: almost not; certainly not
entries.definitionCN: 几乎不；决不，近义副词

entries.definition: not often
entries.definitionCN: 很少；不常，与 hardly ever 的频度义相近

normalIntro.en: Five ways to lock in hardly.
normalIntro.cn: 五个角度锁定 hardly。

normal.en: hardly any
normal.cn: 搭配「hardly any」（几乎没有）是最常见的量级否定。

normal.en: hardly ever
normal.cn: 搭配「hardly ever」（几乎从不）锁定频度用法。

normal.en: hard with -ly
normal.cn: hard 加 -ly 后语义弱化成否定，别按字面理解成「努力地」。

normal.en: hardly any vs some
normal.cn: hardly 是否定词，句中配 any 不配 some。

normal.en: hardly when
normal.cn: 句型「hardly ... when ...」表示「刚……就……」。

abstract.en: Picture light leaking through a door crack: present but almost invisible.
abstract.cn: 想象门缝里漏进的一线光：存在，但几乎看不见——这就是 hardly 的量。

abstract.en: Feel an action pressed down to almost zero.
abstract.cn: 感受一个动作被压到几乎为零：hardly 把动词的分量压扁。

abstract.en: See someone just touching the chair as the phone rings.
abstract.cn: 看到一个人刚碰到椅子电话就响：hardly 表示「刚刚才」。

examples.en: I could hardly hear the teacher from the back row.
examples.cn: 从最后一排我几乎听不见老师的声音。

examples.en: There is hardly any milk left in the bottle.
examples.cn: 瓶子里几乎没剩什么牛奶。

examples.en: She hardly ever watches television these days.
examples.cn: 她这几天几乎从不看电视。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哈的利」——问「哈的利索吗？」答「几乎不利索」：hardly 的意思就是几乎不、简直不。

root: hardly 由 hard（坚硬、用力）加古英语副词后缀 -ly（-lice）构成，本义为「以强硬的方式」。词义在英语史中逐渐弱化，从「用力」到「勉强」再到「几乎不」，属于常见的否定化漂移。

sensesIntro.en: Hardly covers near-negation and the idea of only just.
sensesIntro.cn: hardly 覆盖「近乎否定」与「刚刚才」两层意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crack of light that is almost too faint to see
core.cn: 核心意象：一线光，弱得几乎看不见

branches.en: An action reduced to almost nothing
branches.cn: 被压到几乎为零的动作

branches.en: An event that has just barely happened
branches.cn: 刚刚勉强发生的事件

branches.en: Little quantity, little time
branches.cn: 量极少与时间极短同源

branches.en: Scarcity in amount or frequency
branches.cn: 数量或频度上的稀少

branches.en: Barely finished, already interrupted
branches.cn: 刚完成就被打断的句型感受

intro.en: Hardly is built with the Germanic adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: hardly 用日耳曼副词后缀 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Hardly has no Latin relatives; its family is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: hardly 没有拉丁同族词，词族属日耳曼源。

definition_zh: 失败；不及格；失灵；辜负；缺乏
definition_en: to not succeed, not pass, stop working, disappoint, or be lacking
core_image: 一只伸向目标的手在半空停住，指尖离终点还差一寸
scene: 考试结束铃响，小明放下笔，知道最后一题没答完。 The clock rang, and he knew the last question would fail him.
sceneCN: 这里指「未通过、不及格」，对应第 2 个义项：未达到考核标准；句意为铃响时他明白最后一题没写完会让他不及格。画面要点：铃声、摊开的空白试卷、放下的笔。

pos.zh: 失败；不及格；失灵；辜负；缺乏

derivatives.zh: 失败；故障（动词加名词后缀，指失败这件事或失灵之物）
缺点；弱点（现在分词转名词，指性格上的欠缺）
可靠不衰的（否定前缀加现在分词形容词，指从不落空）
防故障的（复合形容词，指失手也不会酿灾）

senses.title: To not succeed
senses.definition: to not achieve what was attempted
senses.definitionCN: 未能达成所谋之事
senses.example: They failed to reach the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 他们未能登顶。
senses.why: The core image is falling short of a goal; the attempt simply comes up empty.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是够不着目标；尝试最终落空。

senses.title: To not pass a test
senses.definition: to not reach the required standard in a test or course
senses.definitionCN: 在测试或课程中未达标
senses.example: He failed the driving test.
senses.exampleCN: 他没过驾照考试。
senses.why: A standard is a goal; missing it is the same falling short in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 标准即目标；差之毫厘同属「够不着」。

senses.title: To stop working properly
senses.definition: to stop working, or to become weaker
senses.definitionCN: 停止正常运作，或变得衰弱
senses.example: The engine failed in mid-air.
senses.exampleCN: 引擎在半空失灵。
senses.why: A tool that disappoints its user has 'deceived' them; machines fail like false friends.
senses.whyCN: 让使用者失望的工具就是「欺骗」了他们；机器像假朋友一样 fail。

senses.title: To let someone down
senses.definition: to not give someone the help or result they hoped for
senses.definitionCN: 未能给予对方所期望的帮助或结果
senses.example: His memory failed him at the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试时他记不起来了。
senses.why: The root meaning 'deceive' survives here: hoping and not receiving.
senses.whyCN: 词根「欺骗」之义在此存留：期望落空。

senses.title: To be absent or in short supply
senses.definition: to not be present or available when needed
senses.definitionCN: 需要时不在场或不可得
senses.example: The rains failed that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那年雨水短缺。
senses.why: What is missing has, in old French eyes, 'fallen short'; lack is a kind of falling.
senses.whyCN: 在古法语视角里，缺失即「落空」；匮乏是一种跌落。

intro.en: Fail goes back to Latin fallere, 'to deceive or disappoint'; to fail someone is to let their hope fall through.
intro.cn: fail 回溯拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、令人失望）；使某人 fail 就是让其落空。

items.en: Latin fallere meant to deceive; its intransitive use gave 'to be lacking, disappoint'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fallere 意为欺骗；其不及物用法给出「缺失、落空」。

items.en: Old French faillir meant to be lacking, to miss, and grew into falir.
items.cn: 古法语 faillir 意为缺失、未做到。

items.en: Anglo-French failir, failer carried the sense of falling short into England.
items.cn: 盎格鲁法语 failir、failer 把「不足」之义带入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English failen meant to be deficient, to miscarry, to not succeed.
items.cn: 中古英语 failen 意为欠缺、失败、不成功。

items.en: Modern English added the school sense 'to not pass a test' and the noun failure family.
items.cn: 现代英语增加「考试不及格」之义并衍生 failure 一族。

note.en: Look-alikes share spelling or the Latin root fall-; near-meaning words live in the field of not succeeding.
note.cn: 形近组共享拼写或拉丁词根 fall-；近义组处于「未成功」的义场。

entries.definition: to drop downward
entries.definitionCN: 落下；拼写相近但源自古诺斯语，与 fail 不同源

entries.definition: not true, deceiving
entries.definitionCN: 虚假的；与 fail 同出拉丁 fallere

entries.definition: a mistake; originally a deceiving
entries.definitionCN: 过错；同根，古义与欺骗相关

entries.definition: to fail completely, especially publicly
entries.definitionCN: 彻底失败（多指公开场合）

entries.definition: to fall down suddenly
entries.definitionCN: 崩塌；垮掉

entries.definition: to fail a test
entries.definitionCN: 考试不及格（口语）

normalIntro.en: Five grips on the Latin word for disappointing.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语「令人落空」之词的五个抓手。

normal.en: Latin fallere means to deceive or let down, so fail is a hope falling through.
normal.cn: 拉丁 fallere＝欺骗、落空；fail 就是让希望落空。

normal.en: fail to do something is the all-purpose pattern for not managing an action.
normal.cn: fail to do sth 是万能句型：没能做某事。

normal.en: without fail means always, a regular guest at the end of polite letters.
normal.cn: without fail 意为「务必」，信件结尾常客。

normal.en: the noun failure covers both defeat and breakdown, and exams love it.
normal.cn: failure 名词，考纲高频，既是失败也是故障。

normal.en: fail, false, and fault are cousins: all about trickery and empty hands.
normal.cn: fail 与 false、fault 同根，都是「骗与空」。

abstract.en: Failure is a letter sent with no reply, addressed to yourself.
abstract.cn: 失败是一封没有回音的信，收件人是自己。

abstract.en: A pass mark is a bar drawn above your head; failing means never clearing it.
abstract.cn: 不及格是标准线在你头顶画的一道横杠，你没跳过去。

abstract.en: A machine failing feels like a friend missing an appointment: the promised thing simply vanishes.
abstract.cn: 机器失灵像朋友失约：说好的事突然没了。

examples.en: Without fail, the early bus arrives at seven every morning.
examples.cn: 早班车每天早上七点准时到，从不例外。

examples.en: She failed her first driving test but passed the second.
examples.cn: 她第一次驾照考试没过，第二次通过了。

examples.en: The old bridge failed under the heavy truck.
examples.cn: 旧桥在重型卡车下垮了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费哦」——费了半天劲结果哦一声落空，就是 fail。

root: 拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、令人落空）经古法语 faillir 与盎格鲁法语 failir 进入英语。同根词 false（假）、fault（过错）都保留「欺骗」的底色；fail 的各种义项都围绕「落空」展开。

sensesIntro.en: From falling short of a goal outward to tests, machines, people, and scarcity.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「够不着目标」扩展到考试、机器、他人与匮乏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: reaching for something and not getting it.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手去够，却没有够到。

branches.en: THE GOAL MISSED: effort without success.
branches.cn: 未达之标：努力而无成。

branches.en: THE BAR MISSED: not reaching a standard.
branches.cn: 未越之杠：未达标准。

branches.en: THE BROKEN TOOL: machines that stop.
branches.cn: 失灵之器：停摆的机器。

branches.en: THE BROKEN PROMISE: people who disappoint.
branches.cn: 落空的期待：令人失望之人。

branches.en: THE EMPTY HAND: things that are lacking.
branches.cn: 空手：匮乏之物。

intro.en: Fail is the bare French face of the Latin root fall- (deceive); its family is all about trickery and falling short.
intro.cn: fail 是拉丁词根 fall-（欺骗）的法语素颜形态；词族围绕「骗与落空」。

latinIntro.en: Latin fallere, to deceive, seeds false, fault, and fail.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fallere 孕育 false、fault 与 fail。

items.example: false and fail share this root

items.exampleCN: failure 既指失败也指故障

items.example: the fault is in the wiring

definition_zh: 现在的；目前的；出席的；在场的；礼物；提出；呈现
definition_en: existing or happening now; being in a place; a gift; and to give, show, or put something before others
core_image: 一只手把东西伸到另一个人面前：此刻、此地、就在眼前
scene: 年会上，主持人把一个包装好的盒子递到老员工手里，全场鼓掌。 The retiring engineer received a small present from the whole team.
sceneCN: 这里 present 是名词「礼物」（第 3 个义项：送给别人的东西）；句意为即将退休的工程师收到了全队送的一件小礼物。图中可辨识物件：包装盒、彩带、鼓掌的同事。

pos.zh: 现在的；目前的；出席的；在场的

derivatives.zh: 由 present 加 -ation 构成，义为「演示；陈述；颁发」
由 present 加 -ly 构成，义为「不久；目前」
由 present 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「主持人；演示者」
由 present 加 -able 构成，义为「拿得出手的；像样的」

senses.title: Existing or happening now
senses.definition: existing, happening, or being considered at this moment
senses.definitionCN: 此刻存在、发生或正在被考虑的
senses.example: The present situation calls for patience.
senses.exampleCN: 目前的形势需要耐心。
senses.why: Latin praesens describes what stands before the eyes, and what stands before the eyes is by definition what is here now.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praesens 指「摆在眼前的」，而摆在眼前的东西按定义就是此刻的，所以这个词自然有了「现在的」义。

senses.title: Being in a place rather than absent
senses.definition: being in a particular place at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 在某一时间身处某一地点
senses.example: All the members were present at the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 所有成员都出席了投票。
senses.why: The same participle can describe a person as well as a moment: whoever is before us is present in the room.
senses.whyCN: 同一个分词既能修饰时刻，也能修饰人：谁在我们眼前，谁就是「在场的」。

senses.title: A thing given to someone as a gift
senses.definition: something that you give to someone, especially on a special occasion
senses.definitionCN: 赠予某人的东西，尤指在特殊场合
senses.example: She wrapped the present in blue paper.
senses.exampleCN: 她用蓝纸把礼物包了起来。
senses.why: The noun came from the idea of something placed before a person, and a gift is exactly an object set in front of someone to be taken.
senses.whyCN: 名词来自「摆到某人面前的东西」这一想法，而礼物正是被放到对方面前、请对方收下的物件，义项由此固定下来。

senses.title: To offer or submit something formally
senses.definition: to give a plan, report, or proposal to someone in authority for them to consider
senses.definitionCN: 把计划、报告或建议正式交给有权者考虑
senses.example: She presented her proposal to the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她向委员会提出了自己的方案。
senses.why: The Latin verb praesentare meant to place before someone; putting a document before a committee is the modern version of that gesture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 praesentare 意为「放到某人面前」，把文件摆到委员会面前，就是这一动作在现代的版本。

senses.title: To show, display, or perform something
senses.definition: to show something to an audience, or to appear in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 向观众展示某物，或以某种样子出现
senses.example: The theatre will present three new plays this spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家剧院今年春天将上演三部新剧。
senses.why: Once you can place an object before people, you can also place a performance or an image before them, which is how the word reaches stages and screens.
senses.whyCN: 既然能把物件摆到人前，也就能把演出或形象摆到人前，于是这个词走上了舞台与屏幕。

intro.en: Present and presence come from the same Latin participle, but English moved the stress and stretched the meaning from being here to handing something over.
intro.cn: present 与 presence 出自同一个拉丁分词，但英语改变了重音位置，并把词义从「在这里」扩展到「把东西递过去」。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, and it marks whatever is put ahead of a person.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，标示被放到某人面前的东西。

items.en: Esse was the verb to be, and its participle praesens described what is present or at hand.
items.cn: esse 是表示「存在」的动词，它的分词 praesens 描述「在场的、在手边的」东西。

items.en: The verb praesentare meant to place something before someone, and so to offer or show it.
items.cn: 动词 praesentare 意为把某物放到某人面前，因此引申为呈上、展示。

items.en: Old French kept both the adjective of being here and the verb of placing something before another person.
items.cn: 古法语同时保留了「在场的」形容词与「把东西放到别人面前」的动词。

items.en: English puts the stress on the first syllable for the adjective and noun, on the second for the verb, and the meanings spread from time and place to gifts and performances.
items.cn: 现代英语让形容词与名词重音落在第一音节、动词落在第二音节，词义则从时间与地点扩展到礼物与演出。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin participle of being before; the near-meaning group gathers words for gifts, current time, and being somewhere.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「在眼前」的拉丁分词；近义组收礼物、当前时间与到场相关的词。

entries.definition: The state of being in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 在场的状态；出席。

entries.definition: A talk or display given to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 向观众做的演示或展示。

entries.definition: Soon, or at this time.
entries.definitionCN: 不久；此刻。

entries.definition: To stand for something or speak for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 代表某物或替某人说话。

entries.definition: Something given to someone without payment.
entries.definitionCN: 无偿赠予他人的东西。

entries.definition: Happening or existing now.
entries.definitionCN: 现在发生或存在的。

entries.definition: To be at an event.
entries.definitionCN: 到场参加活动。

entries.definition: To give or propose something.
entries.definitionCN: 给予或提出某物。

normalIntro.en: One Latin participle gives both the thing that is here and the act of putting something in front of someone, and English separates them by stress.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁分词同时给出「在这里的东西」与「把东西放到别人面前的动作」，英语用重音把两者分开。

normal.en: The adjective and noun stress the first syllable, the verb the second: PREZ-unt for a thing, pri-ZENT for an action.
normal.cn: 形容词与名词重音在第一音节，动词在第二音节：指物时读前重，指动作时读后重。

normal.en: Present and presence share the Latin participle praesens, so both begin with the idea of being before someone.
normal.cn: present 与 presence 共用一个拉丁分词，起点都是「在某人面前」。

normal.en: Present as a gift is the object placed before a person, the same gesture as presenting a report.
normal.cn: 作「礼物」的 present 是被放到人前的物件，与呈交报告是同一个动作。

normal.en: At present is a fixed phrase for this moment, built on the time sense of the adjective.
normal.cn: at present 是表示「此刻」的固定说法，建立在形容词的时间义上。

normal.en: Presentation and presenter add endings to the verb, naming the act and the person who performs it.
normal.cn: presentation 与 presenter 给动词加后缀，分别命名行为与执行的人。

abstract.en: One word holds a moment, a place, a gift and a stage, because all of them are put in front of someone.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装下时刻、地点、礼物与舞台，因为它们都被摆到了某人面前。

abstract.en: The stress moves like the meaning: first syllable for what is here, second for what you do with it.
abstract.cn: 重音随词义移动：前重指「在这里的东西」，后重指「你拿它做什么」。

abstract.en: A present is only a present once it is handed over, which is why the noun and the verb share a shape.
abstract.cn: 礼物只有递出去才成为礼物，所以名词与动词共用一个形状。

examples.en: The present situation calls for patience.
examples.cn: 目前的形势需要耐心。

examples.en: She presented her proposal to the committee.
examples.cn: 她向委员会提出了自己的方案。

examples.en: He gave her a small present before leaving.
examples.cn: 他临走前送了她一件小礼物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读起来像「pre（先）+ sent（送）」：先送到人前的是礼物，先摆到人前的是方案，present 就是「呈到面前」。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ esse（存在）→ praesens（在眼前的），经古法语 present 进入英语；形容词与名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something placed before someone: time and place first, then the gift put in front of a person, then the act of laying a plan or a show before others.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「摆到某人面前」：先是时间与地点上的「在眼前」，再是递到面前的礼物，最后是把方案或演出摆到别人面前。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand holding something out toward another person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西伸到另一个人面前。

branches.en: a clock showing this very minute
branches.cn: 钟面停在此刻这一分钟

branches.en: a full row of chairs with nobody missing
branches.cn: 一排椅子坐满，无人缺席

branches.en: a wrapped box held out with both hands
branches.cn: 双手递出的包装盒

branches.en: a folder laid on the committee table
branches.cn: 放在委员桌上的文件夹

branches.en: a curtain rising on a new play
branches.cn: 新戏开演时升起的幕布

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle of being, its verb of placing before, and the English endings that name the act, the person and the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「存在」的拉丁分词、表示「放到面前」的动词，以及命名行为、人物与性质的英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the act of showing or giving

definition_zh: 极好的；卓越的；优秀的；出色的
definition_en: extremely good; outstanding in quality
core_image: 高出众人一头的那个人：在一排人里，他被拔得最高、看得最清
scene: 运动会上全班都在跳高，杆子一次次升高，最后只剩他轻松越过最高一格，看台上传来喊声： That was an excellent jump!
sceneCN: 这里 excellent 指「质量上乘、高出一般」（第 1 个义项：品质极佳的）；句意为那一跳非常出色。

derivatives.zh: 卓越；优点（excellent 的名词形式，义为「高出常格的品德或品质」）
超过；胜过（同源，义为「越过边界」）
胜过；擅长（同根动词，义为「高出他人」）

senses.title: Of outstanding quality
senses.definition: extremely good in quality or standard
senses.definitionCN: 质量或水准非常高
senses.example: That was an excellent jump!
senses.exampleCN: 那一跳跳得非常出色！
senses.why: The root image is being lifted above the line: what is excellent stands higher than the ordinary grade around it.
senses.whyCN: 词根画面是「被抬到线以上」：excellent 的东西比周围普通水准高出一截。

senses.title: Showing great skill or ability
senses.definition: showing a very high level of skill or ability
senses.definitionCN: 技艺或能力达到很高的水平
senses.example: She is excellent at explaining difficult ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 她特别擅长把难懂的想法讲明白。
senses.why: Being above the line in performance, not just in material quality, extends the image to people and their skills.
senses.whyCN: 「高出线」不只是东西的质量，也可以落在人的表现上，于是延伸到技艺层面。

senses.title: Used as strong approval
senses.definition: used to show strong approval or agreement, often as a single word
senses.definitionCN: 常以单词形式单独喊出，表示强烈赞同
senses.example: Excellent! We will go with your plan.
senses.exampleCN: 太好了！就按你的方案办。
senses.why: When the judgment is spoken alone, the comparative image stays but the sentence shrinks to pure praise.
senses.whyCN: 判断被单独喊出时，「高出一线」的画面还在，句子却缩成纯粹的赞许。

senses.title: Of very good health or condition
senses.definition: in very good health or physical condition
senses.definitionCN: 身体或物品处于很好的状态
senses.example: The old car is in excellent condition.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧车车况极佳。
senses.why: The line being compared against is the expected state; staying well above it is still the same image of being raised up.
senses.whyCN: 比较线是预期状态，状态远高于预期，仍是「被抬高」这一意象。

intro.en: Excellent climbs out of Latin via French, and its root means literally "to rise high, to outdo".
intro.cn: excellent 经法语源自拉丁语，词根本义是「升高、超出」。

items.en: Latin excellere meant "to rise up, to be eminent", from ex- (out, up) + a base -cellere related to celsus "high".
items.cn: 拉丁语 excellere 意为「升高、出众」，由 ex-（向上、向外）加词干构成，词干与 celsus「高」同源。

items.en: The picture is of something being lifted above a surrounding level, which is why the word always implies comparison.
items.cn: 画面是某物被抬到周围水准之上，因此这个词天生含比较意味。

items.en: Old French carried it as excellent, an adjective already in learned use.
items.cn: 古法语以 excellent 的形式继承，当时已是书面语形容词。

items.en: Middle English took it from French in the fourteenth century, first meaning "surpassing, excelling".
items.cn: 十四世纪中古英语从法语借入，最初义为「胜过、超越」。

items.en: Modern English settled it as the everyday top grade of praise, from objects to skills to bare exclamations.
items.cn: 现代英语把它定为日常赞美的最高档，从物品、技艺到单独的感叹都在用。

note.en: Nearby words share the spelling family or the idea of standing above the ordinary.
note.cn: 相邻的词与 excellent 同族，或同样有「高出寻常」的意思。

entries.definitionCN: 擅长；胜过（同根动词）

entries.definition: the quality of being outstanding
entries.definitionCN: 卓越；优点（同根名词）

entries.definition: to go beyond a limit or number
entries.definitionCN: 超过（同源，义为「越界」）

entries.definition: not including; but not

entries.definition: clearly much better than others

entries.definition: of the highest quality

normalIntro.en: Five associations grounded in the real root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 五条建立在真实词根与词族上的联想。

normal.en: ex- (up/out) + cell- (high): something raised above the line.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex-（向上）+ 词根 cell-（高）：某物被抬到线以上。

normal.en: Excel is the verb: he excels at maths, so his work is excellent.
normal.cn: excel 是动词：他数学出众，所以他的作业 excellent。

normal.en: Excellence is the noun: the school prizes academic excellence.
normal.cn: excellence 是名词：学校重视学术卓越。

normal.en: Exceed shares the rising image: the result exceeds all hopes.
normal.cn: exceed 共享「升高」的画面：结果超出所有期望。

normal.en: Shouting "Excellent!" is giving the top grade out loud.
normal.cn: 喊一声 "Excellent!" 就是大声打出最高分。

abstract.en: Picture a bar being raised in a high-jump contest until one jumper clears it easily.
abstract.cn: 想象跳高比赛的横杆不断升高，最后只剩一人轻松越过。

abstract.en: Everything ordinary sits under the line; the excellent thing stands above it in clear air.
abstract.cn: 平常的东西都在线以下，卓越的东西立在清朗的高处。

abstract.en: Praise is a ranking act: to call something excellent is to lift it in words.
abstract.cn: 称赞是一种排名：说某物 excellent，就是用语言把它抬高。

examples.en: That was an excellent jump!
examples.cn: 那一跳跳得非常出色！

examples.en: She is excellent at explaining difficult ideas.
examples.cn: 她特别擅长把难懂的想法讲明白。

examples.en: The old car is in excellent condition.
examples.cn: 这辆旧车车况极佳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克塞乐」——爱到可以塞满快乐，因为好得不得了，简直「爱克塞乐」。

root: 源自拉丁语 excellere「升高、出众」，由 ex-（向上、向外）+ 词干 -cellere 构成，词干与 celsus「高」同源；一般认为原义与「被抬高」的画面相关。经古法语进入中古英语。

sensesIntro.en: From being raised above the ordinary line, the word spreads to skills, condition, and bare spoken praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「高出寻常一线」出发，扩展到技艺、状态乃至脱口而出的赞许。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lifted above the common line
core.cn: 核心意象：被抬到众人所在的普通线以上

branches.en: quality or condition above the norm
branches.cn: 质量或状态超出常规

branches.en: skill raised above the crowd
branches.cn: 技艺高出一众

branches.en: praise spoken as a single lifted word
branches.cn: 赞许单独成词喊出

branches.en: excelling implies comparison
branches.cn: 卓越天生含比较

branches.en: high performance earns admiration
branches.cn: 高表现赢得赞许

intro.en: The family keeps the Latin ex- (up, out) plus the high-root, with regular English suffixes.
intro.cn: 词族保留拉丁 ex-（向上）与「高」词根，再接规则英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cousins that carry the rising root.
latinIntro.cn: 带「升高」词根的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 驾驶；驱使；驱动；驱赶； drives；干劲；车道
definition_en: to operate a vehicle so that it moves, or to force someone or something to act or move
core_image: 手握方向盘，把车推向前进
scene: 清晨的公路上薄雾未散，爸爸坐进车里发动了引擎。 My father will drive me to school before his first meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 drive 是「开车送、驾驶」（第 1 个义项：操作车辆使其移动）；句意：爸爸会在第一个会议之前开车送我去学校。

derivatives.zh: drive 加表示者的后缀 er 构成，义为「司机；驱动器」
drive 的现在分词转形容词，义为「行驶的；猛烈的」

senses.title: Operate a vehicle
senses.definition: to control a car, bus, or other vehicle and make it move
senses.definitionCN: 操控汽车、公共汽车等车辆使其行驶
senses.example: She drives the children to school every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上开车送孩子们上学。
senses.why: Driving is the oldest sense: the wheel is held and the vehicle is pushed forward.
senses.whyCN: 驾驶是最早的义项：手握住方向盘，把车辆向前推。

senses.title: Force someone to act
senses.definition: to push a person to do something, often with strong emotion
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地推动某人做某事，常带强烈情绪
senses.example: Hunger drove the family to leave their village.
senses.exampleCN: 饥饿驱使这家人离开村庄。
senses.why: The image of pushing a vehicle forward grows into pushing a person toward action.
senses.whyCN: 把车辆往前推的意象，长出了把人推向行动的引申义。

senses.title: Power a machine
senses.definition: to provide the energy that makes a machine or system work
senses.definitionCN: 为机器或系统提供使其运转的能量
senses.example: The engine drives the wheels of the truck.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机驱动卡车的车轮。
senses.why: A machine, like a car, is moved by a force acting on it, so the same word serves.
senses.whyCN: 机器像车一样被外力推动，所以共用同一个词。

senses.title: Push animals away
senses.definition: to make animals or people move in a direction by force
senses.definitionCN: 用力使动物或人朝某个方向移动
senses.example: The farmer drove the sheep into the pen.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫把羊赶进围栏。
senses.why: Herdsmen literally drove cattle along roads long before cars existed.
senses.whyCN: 早在汽车出现之前，牧人就已经在路上驱赶牛群了。

senses.title: Strong energy or desire
senses.definition: a strong inner force that makes a person want to act
senses.definitionCN: 使人想要行动的强烈内在力量
senses.example: Her drive to win impressed the coach.
senses.exampleCN: 她的求胜干劲给教练留下深刻印象。
senses.why: The pushing force inside a machine becomes the pushing force inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 机器内部的推动力，变成了人内心的推动力。

senses.title: A road for vehicles
senses.definition: a short road leading to a house, or a wide street
senses.definitionCN: 通向住宅的短车道，或宽阔的街道
senses.example: A car stopped at the end of the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆车停在长车道尽头。
senses.why: The road built for driving took the verb as its name.
senses.whyCN: 专供行驶的路，便用这个动词命名。

intro.en: Drive is an old Germanic word about pushing things forward, first animals, then vehicles, then machines and minds.
intro.cn: drive 是一个古老的日耳曼词，核心是「把东西向前推」：先是牲畜，后是车辆，再到机器与人心。

items.en: The Proto-Germanic root *driban meant to push or drive forward, used of driving cattle.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语词根 *driban 意为向前推、驱赶，用于驱赶牲畜。

items.en: Old English drīfan meant to force to move, to urge onward, for both animals and people.
items.cn: 古英语 drīfan 意为迫使移动、催促前行，对象既包括牲畜也包括人。

items.en: In Middle English the word covered forcing people onward and pushing wheeled vehicles.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，这个词既指迫使他人前行，也指推动带轮的车辆。

items.en: With railways and cars, drive settled as the main word for operating a vehicle, then spread to engines and motivation.
items.cn: 随铁路与汽车兴起，drive 成为操作车辆的主要用词，进而扩展到发动机与动机。

items.en: The Latin cognate graidhi, to step forward, is a distant reconstructed relative behind the pushing idea.
items.cn: 拉丁语同源词 graidhi（向前迈步）是「推」这一意象背后较远的重构同源词。

note.en: These words stand near drive in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 drive 相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 司机；驱动器

entries.definition: past participle of drive; strongly motivated
entries.definitionCN: drive 的过去分词；有强烈动力的

entries.definition: to press something to make it move
entries.definitionCN: 推；推动

entries.definitionCN: 敦促；催促

normalIntro.en: Use the pushing-wheel picture and the drive family.
normalIntro.cn: 用「推轮前行」的画面和 drive 词族来记。

normal.en: drive a car is the school-day first meaning everyone learns.
normal.cn: drive a car 是课堂上学的第一层意思。

normal.en: drove, driven is an irregular set worth chanting out loud.
normal.cn: drove、driven 是不规则变化，值得大声念熟。

normal.en: drive someone crazy pushes a person to the edge of patience.
normal.cn: drive someone crazy 是把人推到忍耐的边缘。

normal.en: A driveway is the path a car drives along to the door.
normal.cn: driveway 就是汽车驶到家门口的那条道。

normal.en: Hunger can drive you to the kitchen like a hidden engine.
normal.cn: 饥饿像一台隐藏的发动机，驱使你冲进厨房。

abstract.en: Feel your hands gripping a wheel and pressing forward.
abstract.cn: 感受双手握紧方向盘、向前推进的力量。

abstract.en: Picture an engine pushing a whole family toward a new city.
abstract.cn: 想象一台发动机推动一家人奔向新的城市。

abstract.en: See hunger as a hand at your back, pushing you onward.
abstract.cn: 把饥饿想象成一只在你背后推你前行的手。

examples.cn: 他每天开着一辆旧卡车穿过农场。

examples.en: The desire to win drove her to train before sunrise.
examples.cn: 求胜的欲望驱使她在日出前训练。

examples.en: That small motor drives the fan inside the machine.
examples.cn: 那台小马达驱动机器里的风扇。
