root: 来自原始日耳曼语词根 *driban（向前推、驱赶），古英语 drīfan（迫使移动）；本义为驱赶牲畜，后引申为驾驶车辆、驱动机器与驱使人。

sensesIntro.en: Drive starts with pushing animals forward, then grows into vehicles, machines, people and desire.
sensesIntro.cn: drive 从驱赶牲畜出发，长出驾驶、驱动、驱使与干劲等义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a firm hand pushing a wheel forward
core.cn: 核心意象：一只坚定的手把轮子向前推

branches.en: The vehicle made to move
branches.cn: 被开动起来的车辆

branches.en: The person or animal pushed onward
branches.cn: 被推着前行的人或牲畜

branches.en: The machine powered from behind
branches.cn: 被后方供能驱动的机器

branches.en: The pushing force inside a heart
branches.cn: 藏在心里的推动力

branches.en: The road built for driving
branches.cn: 专供行驶的道路

intro.en: Drive sits in a small Germanic pushing family with the -er and -ing endings.
intro.cn: drive 处在一个小小的日耳曼「推」词族里，带上 er 与 ing 两种尾缀。

latinIntro.en: Drive is Germanic in origin, so it has no Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: drive 源自日耳曼语，因此没有拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: a road for driving to a house
one who or that which does

items.meaningCN: 做白日梦的人（对比 -er 用法）

items.meaning: to grow strongly (same old root family)
items.meaningCN: 兴旺；茁壮成长（同古老词族）
items.exampleCN: 植物在阳光下茁壮生长。

definition_zh: 交流；沟通；传达；通信；连通
definition_en: to share information, ideas or feelings with others
core_image: 把心里的消息放进对方心里的小信箱
scene: 课间，两个同学用手势帮新同学指路。 New students can communicate with signs when words fail.
sceneCN: 这里 communicate 是「交流」（第 1 个义项：传递信息）；句意是词语不通时新同学可以用手势交流。

derivatives.zh: 由 communicate 加 -ion 构成，义为「交流；通信」
由 communicate 加 -ive 构成，义为「爱说话的；善于沟通的」
由 communicate 加 -or 构成，义为「交流者；沟通者」

senses.title: To share information
senses.definition: to give and receive news, ideas or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 交换消息、想法或感受
senses.example: We communicate by WeChat every day.
senses.exampleCN: 我们每天用微信交流。
senses.why: A message leaves one mind and lands in another.
senses.whyCN: 消息从一颗心出发，落进另一颗心。

senses.title: To make feelings known
senses.definition: to show what you think or feel without always using words
senses.definitionCN: 不必总用语言就能让人明白你的想法或感受
senses.example: Babies communicate hunger by crying.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿用哭声表达饥饿。
senses.why: A face or a gesture can carry meaning too.
senses.whyCN: 表情和手势同样能传递意义。

senses.title: To be connected by paths or signals
senses.definition: two places or systems joined so things can pass between
senses.definitionCN: 两地或系统相连使信息、道路互通
senses.example: The island communicates with the city by ferry.
senses.exampleCN: 小岛靠渡轮与城市连通。
senses.why: When a road or signal opens, places begin to share.
senses.whyCN: 道路或信号一通，两地便开始互通。

intro.en: To communicate once meant to make common.
intro.cn: communicate 的本义是「使其共有」。

items.en: Latin communis means shared by all, common.
items.cn: 拉丁语 communis 意为人人共享的、共同的。

items.en: Communicare meant to share, to make something common to others.
items.cn: communicare 意为分享，使某物为他人共有。

items.en: The past form communicatus kept this sense.
items.cn: 过去分词 communicatus 保留此义。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语于十六世纪吸收该动词。

items.en: Today it mostly means sending and receiving messages.
items.cn: 如今它主要指发送和接收信息。

note.en: The communis family about sharing.
note.cn: 表示共享的 communis 词族。

entries.definition: noun: the act of communicating
entries.definitionCN: 交流；通信（同根名词）

entries.definition: willing to talk and share
entries.definitionCN: 爱交流的

entries.definition: a group sharing a place or life
entries.definitionCN: 社区；群体

entries.definition: shared by everyone in a group
entries.definitionCN: 公共的

entries.definition: to speak with someone
entries.definitionCN: 交谈

entries.definition: to give and receive in turn
entries.definitionCN: 交换

entries.definition: a sign carrying a message
entries.definitionCN: 信号

entries.definition: to pay no attention
entries.definitionCN: 忽视

normalIntro.en: See community inside: sharing makes it work.
normalIntro.cn: 在词里看见 community：共享让一切运转。

normal.en: communicate = share with others.
normal.cn: communicate 意为与他人分享。

normal.en: communicate with somebody needs listening too.
normal.cn: communicate with 某人也需要倾听。

normal.en: communication includes emails, calls and signs.
normal.cn: communication 包括邮件、电话与手势。

normal.en: communicative people love to talk.
normal.cn: communicative 的人爱交流。

normal.en: community members communicate daily.
normal.cn: 社区成员天天交流。

abstract.en: Picture two paper cups joined by a string telephone.
abstract.cn: 想象两个纸杯连成土电话。

abstract.en: Picture a message flying from one phone to another.
abstract.cn: 想象消息在手机之间飞行。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge where walkers share news on the way.
abstract.cn: 想象桥上行人一路互传消息。

examples.en: Good friends communicate openly about problems.
examples.cn: 好朋友会坦诚交流问题。

examples.en: Dolphins seem to communicate with clicks and whistles.
examples.cn: 海豚似乎用咔嗒声和哨声交流。

examples.en: We communicated our thanks with a big hand-made card.
examples.cn: 我们用一张大大的手工卡片表达谢意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「渴缪你给」——渴望交流时，缪缪用眼神「给」你信号，你来我往，所以「渴缪你给」= communicate。

root: 拉丁语 communis（共同的）→ communicare（共享）→ communicatus → 英语 communicate。community、common、commune 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Making things common: words, feelings and roads.
sensesIntro.cn: 把话语、情感和道路变得共通。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: turning my thought into our thought
core.cn: 核心意象：把「我的想法」变成「我们的想法」

branches.en: Messages passed and received
branches.cn: 信息的传递与接收

branches.en: Feelings shown without words
branches.cn: 无需言语的表达

branches.en: Places joined by roads and signals
branches.cn: 被道路与信号连接的地方

branches.en: Friendship built on talk
branches.cn: 建立在交流上的友谊

branches.en: Networks that keep us linked
branches.cn: 把我们连在一起的网络

intro.en: Commun- means common; the endings add roles.
intro.cn: commun- 表示共同；后缀补充角色。

latinIntro.en: Latin communis powers this whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 communis 支撑整个词族。

items.example: Communication is the act of sharing.
Our community cleans the park monthly.
items.exampleCN: 我们的社区每月清洁公园。

definition_zh: 报纸；一份报纸；报社
definition_en: a printed publication, usually issued daily or weekly, containing news, articles and advertisements
core_image: 折叠的报纸摊在餐桌上，一角被咖啡杯压住，露出半截头条
scene: 早餐桌上一杯咖啡压着摊开的报纸，父亲边喝边翻到体育版。 He reads a newspaper every morning before work.
sceneCN: 这里 newspaper 是「报纸」（第 1 个义项：刊载新闻的印刷出版物）；句意为他每天上班前都读一份报纸。图中可辨识物件：咖啡杯、摊开的报纸、餐桌。

derivatives.zh: 由 news 与 print 复合，义为「新闻纸」
由 newspaper 与 man 复合，义为「报人；男记者」
由 newspaper 与 woman 复合，义为「女报人；女记者」

senses.title: A printed publication with news
senses.definition: a set of printed sheets, usually published daily or weekly, containing news, articles and advertisements
senses.definitionCN: 通常每日或每周出版、刊载新闻、文章与广告的一套印刷纸张
senses.example: The newspaper printed the story on its front page.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报纸把这条新闻登在了头版。
senses.why: The compound joins news with paper, so the name literally points to the sheets that carry the reports.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 news 与 paper 拼在一起，字面上就指向承载报道的那些纸张。

senses.title: A single copy or issue
senses.definition: one copy or one day's issue of such a publication
senses.definitionCN: 这样一份出版物的一份或某一期
senses.example: She bought a newspaper from the stand on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 她从街角的报刊亭买了一份报纸。
senses.why: Once the sheets become a product, the same word can count them one by one in a reader's hands.
senses.whyCN: 当这些纸张变成商品，同一个词就能在读者手里把它们一份一份地数出来。

senses.title: The organization that publishes it
senses.definition: the company or office that produces a newspaper
senses.definitionCN: 生产这份报纸的公司或办公机构
senses.example: He has worked for the same newspaper for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在同一家报社工作了二十年。
senses.why: A paper is also the people who write and print it, so the word slides from the object to the institution behind it.
senses.whyCN: 一份报纸也指写它、印它的那些人，于是词义从物件滑到它背后的机构。

intro.en: Newspaper joins the English word news to paper, a word that came from Latin through Old French and named the material before it named the publication.
intro.cn: newspaper 把英语的 news 与 paper 组合起来；paper 经古法语来自拉丁语，先指材料，后指出版物。

items.en: Papyrus was the writing reed of the ancient world and gave Latin its word for paper.
items.cn: papyrus 是古代用来书写的芦苇，也是拉丁语中「纸」一词的来源。

items.en: Old French shortened papyrus into papier, the material on which words were written.
items.cn: 古法语把 papyrus 缩成 papier，指书写文字所用的材料。

items.en: Middle English paper named the material and later a sheet or a document made from it.
items.cn: 中古英语 paper 指纸张材料，后来也指用纸做成的一页或一份文件。

items.en: News and paper were combined into newspaper for the printed sheets that carried reports.
items.cn: news 与 paper 组合成 newspaper，指承载报道的印刷纸张。

items.en: Modern English uses newspaper for the printed product, a single issue and the company that publishes it.
items.cn: 现代英语用 newspaper 指印刷品、单份报纸，也指出版它的公司。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on news or on the paper compound; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of periodical publication.
note.cn: 形近组收以 news 或 paper 复合而成的词；近义组收其他类型的定期出版物。

entries.definition: Information about recent events; the first half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 关于近期事件的信息；这个复合词的前半部分。

entries.definition: The material made for writing and printing; the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 用于书写和印刷的材料；这个复合词的后半部分。

entries.definition: The cheap paper used for printing newspapers.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷报纸所用的廉价纸张。

entries.definition: A small stall where newspapers are sold.
entries.definitionCN: 出售报纸的小摊；报刊亭。

entries.definition: A periodical, often more serious or specialised than a newspaper.
entries.definitionCN: 定期刊物，常比报纸更严肃或更专业。

entries.definition: A small-format newspaper focused on sensation and pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 以小版面、耸动内容和图片为主的小报。

entries.definition: A large-format newspaper known for serious reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 以大版面、严肃报道著称的报纸。

entries.definition: Any publication that appears at regular intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 任何定期出版的刊物。

normalIntro.en: The word is a plain compound of news and paper, and its family keeps combining the report with the material or the place that sells it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 news 与 paper 的直接复合，词族不断把「报道」与材料或售卖地点结合起来。

normal.en: news plus paper equals the paper that carries the news.
normal.cn: news 加 paper 等于承载新闻的那种纸。

normal.en: Paper goes back to Latin papyrus, the reed once used for writing.
normal.cn: paper 可追到拉丁语 papyrus，那是古时用来书写的芦苇。

normal.en: One newspaper, two newspapers: count the physical copies with a plural.
normal.cn: one newspaper、two newspapers：用复数来数一份份实物。

normal.en: The newspaper can also mean the company, and then it takes a singular verb.
normal.cn: the newspaper 也可指公司，这时它接单数动词。

normal.en: The usual partners are daily newspaper, local newspaper and newspaper article.
normal.cn: 常见搭配有 daily newspaper、local newspaper 与 newspaper article。

abstract.en: A newspaper is news that has been given a body of paper and a daily habit.
abstract.cn: 报纸就是给新闻配上一副纸做的身体，再养成每天阅读的习惯。

abstract.en: The same word covers the object, the single copy and the institution because a paper exists only while all three hold together.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指物件、单份与机构，因为只有三者抱在一起，一份报纸才成立。

abstract.en: Every folded page is a day's worth of the world pressed flat.
abstract.cn: 每一页折起的纸，都是一天世界被压平的形状。

examples.en: He reads a newspaper every morning before work.
examples.cn: 他每天上班前都读一份报纸。

examples.en: The local newspaper sent a reporter to the school fair.
examples.cn: 地方报纸派了一名记者去学校集市。

examples.en: She wrapped the old plates in newspaper before putting them in the box.
examples.cn: 她用旧报纸把盘子包好，再放进箱子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「纽斯陪珀」——「纽斯」是新事的声音，「陪珀」是纸页的声响，合起来就是报纸。

root: news（新闻）与 paper（纸）复合；paper 源自拉丁语 papyrus（纸莎草），经古法语 papier 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is printed sheets carrying reports; the senses then move to the single copy and to the company that produces it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是承载报道的印刷纸张；义项由此转到单份报纸，再转到生产它的公司。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded paper on the breakfast table, one corner held down by a coffee cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：早餐桌上折叠的报纸，一角被咖啡杯压住。

branches.en: a front page lying open beside a cup
branches.cn: 摊在杯子旁边的头版

branches.en: a coin handed over for one copy
branches.cn: 买一份报纸递出的一枚硬币

branches.en: a newsroom full of ringing phones
branches.cn: 电话响个不停的编辑部

branches.en: the same sheets as a product and as one purchase
branches.cn: 同样的纸张，既是产品，也是一次购买

branches.en: a copy in a hand and the office that made it
branches.cn: 手里的一份报纸与做出它的报馆

intro.en: The word is a compound of news and paper, and its family keeps pairing the report with print, sellers and the people who make it.
intro.cn: 这个词是 news 与 paper 的复合，词族不断把报道与印刷、售卖者和制作的人配在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin papyrus names the reed that became paper, and it is the one reliable Latin ancestor behind this compound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 papyrus 指后来变成纸的那种芦苇，是这个复合词背后唯一可靠的拉丁来源。

items.meaning: material made for writing and printing
the reed used as writing material
the cheap paper used for newspapers
a man who works for a newspaper

latinEntries.meaning: the papyrus reed used as writing material
latinEntries.meaningCN: 用作书写材料的纸莎草

definition_zh: 习俗；风俗；习惯；海关
definition_en: a usual way of doing things in a group or place
core_image: 大家年年照着做、代代传下来的固定做法
scene: 春节前全家大扫除，奶奶说这是老规矩，年年都不能少。 Keeping the doors clean before the new year is a Chinese custom.
sceneCN: 这里 custom 是「习俗」（第 1 个义项：群体沿袭的固定做法）；句意是春节前扫除门庭是中国的一项习俗。

derivatives.zh: 由 custom 加 -ary 构成，义为「惯常的；合乎习俗的」
与 custom 同源，由 custom 加 -er 构成，义为「顾客」
由 ac- 加 custom 构成，义为「使习惯于」
custom 的复数形式转义，义为「海关」

senses.title: A shared way of doing things
senses.definition: an action or way of behaving that a group has followed for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体长期沿袭的做法或行为方式
senses.example: It is a custom in our town to light lanterns on the last night of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 在除夕夜点灯笼是我们镇上的习俗。
senses.why: Doing the same thing together year after year presses a groove, and the groove is a custom.
senses.whyCN: 年年一起做同样的事会压出一道「沟」，这道沟就是习俗。

senses.title: A personal habit
senses.definition: a usual practice of one person, often formal in style
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的惯常做法，语气较正式
senses.example: It is my custom to review notes before going to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 睡前复习笔记是我的习惯。
senses.why: What a group repeats is custom; what one person repeats borrows the same word.
senses.whyCN: 群体重复的是习俗，个人重复的做法也借用同一个词。

senses.title: The government office for imported goods
senses.definition: the place at ports and borders where officials check goods brought into a country
senses.definitionCN: 港口、边境检查入境货物的机构
senses.example: We waited an hour at customs before our bags were checked.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在海关等了一个小时才检查完行李。
senses.why: Declared goods follow fixed rules, so the checking office took the word for fixed practice.
senses.whyCN: 申报货物要按固定规则办理，检查机构便沿用了「固定做法」这个词。

intro.en: Custom traces back to a Latin verb for becoming used to something.
intro.cn: custom 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「习惯于」的动词。

items.en: consuescere meant to accustom oneself; the noun consuetudo meant habit or usage.
items.cn: 拉丁语 consuescere 意为使自己习惯；名词 consuetudo 指习惯、惯例。

items.en: Old French kept it as custume, meaning habit or usage.
items.cn: 古法语保留为 custume，意为习惯、惯例。

items.en: English took custume around the twelfth century, first for a settled practice.
items.cn: 英语约在十二世纪吸收 custume，最初指固定做法。

items.en: Because traders paid regular dues, customs came to name the dues and the office that collected them.
items.cn: 因为商人定期缴纳通行税，customs 便转指税款和征税机构，即海关。

items.en: Today custom covers folkways, personal habits and the customs house at the airport.
items.cn: 如今 custom 涵盖民俗、个人习惯和机场的海关。

note.en: These words belong to the custom family or name repeated behaviour.
note.cn: 这些词属于 custom 词族，或指重复出现的行为。

entries.definition: usual according to custom
entries.definitionCN: 惯常的

entries.definition: a person who buys things; from the same Latin root
entries.definitionCN: 顾客（同源词）

entries.definition: to make used to something
entries.definitionCN: 使习惯于

entries.definition: clothes worn for a play or party; spelled close to custom, different root
entries.definitionCN: 戏服；化装服（拼写近似，词源不同）

entries.definition: a custom passed down through generations
entries.definitionCN: 传统；世代相传的习俗

entries.definition: something you do often without thinking
entries.definitionCN: 习惯

entries.definition: a usual or accepted way of doing things
entries.definitionCN: 惯例；做法

entries.definition: a set of actions done in a fixed order, often formal
entries.definitionCN: 仪式；例行程序

entries.definition: an accepted way of behaving in society
entries.definitionCN: 惯例；常规

normalIntro.en: Use the custom family and travel words to remember it.
normalIntro.cn: 用 custom 词族和出行词汇来记。

normal.en: custom + ary = customary, done as usual.
normal.cn: custom + ary ＝ customary（惯常的）。

normal.en: ac- + custom = accustom, to make used to.
normal.cn: ac- + custom ＝ accustom（使习惯于）。

normal.en: customer keeps the same root: regular buyers follow the shop's customs.
normal.cn: customer 同源：常客按店铺的惯例来买东西。

normal.en: At the airport, customs is plural in use: go through customs.
normal.cn: 在机场 customs 用复数形式：go through customs（过海关）。

normal.en: Watch the spelling: custom, not costum. Costume means clothes.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：custom，别写成 costum；costume 是服装。

abstract.en: Picture the same lantern hung on the same night every year.
abstract.cn: 想象每年同一个夜晚挂起同一盏灯笼。

abstract.en: Feel the groove a path wears into grass after many walkers.
abstract.cn: 体会许多人走过之后在草地上踩出的小道。

abstract.en: Hear the stamp at the border that lets fixed rules pass your bag.
abstract.cn: 听边检的章落下，固定的规则放行你的行李。

examples.en: Giving red envelopes is a custom at Chinese new year.
examples.cn: 过年发红包是中国的一项习俗。

examples.en: Each class has its own customs, such as cleaning the board after lessons.

definition_zh: 同意；答应；意见一致；相符
definition_en: to share the same opinion, or to say yes, or to match something
core_image: 几个人点头表示赞同
scene: 小组讨论时，几个同学一起点头表示赞同。 We agree with the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 agree 是「同意」（第 1 个义项：持相同意见）；句意为我们都同意这个计划。

senses.title: To share the same view
senses.definition: to have the same opinion as someone
senses.definitionCN: 与某人有相同的看法
senses.example: I agree with you.
senses.exampleCN: 我同意你。
senses.why: Agree comes from a French phrase meaning to bring to one mind, so two people sharing a view agree.
senses.whyCN: agree 来自法语短语「使合意」，两人看法合到一处，就是同意。

senses.title: To reach a shared decision
senses.definition: to come to a shared decision after talking
senses.definitionCN: 谈过之后共同做出决定
senses.example: The two sides agreed on a price.
senses.exampleCN: 双方谈定了一个价格。
senses.why: When both sides move to one mind about a deal, they reach an agreement.
senses.whyCN: 双方谈到同一个意上，就是达成一致。

senses.title: To match a fact
senses.definition: to be the same as another account or fact
senses.definitionCN: 与另一种说法或事实一致
senses.example: The two accounts do not agree.
senses.exampleCN: 两种说法并不相符。
senses.why: The idea of being of one mind was applied to facts, so matching accounts agree.
senses.whyCN: 把「合」用在说法与事实之间，就是相符。

senses.title: To say yes to a plan
senses.definition: to accept a plan or a suggestion
senses.definitionCN: 接受一项计划或提议
senses.example: We agreed to the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 我们赞成这个新计划。
senses.why: Saying yes to a plan is the everyday form of being of one mind with it.
senses.whyCN: 对一项计划说好，就是日常语境里的赞成。

senses.title: To suit the body
senses.definition: to be good for a person's health
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的身体有益
senses.example: Too much sugar does not agree with me.
senses.exampleCN: 糖吃太多对我不合适。
senses.why: In health talk, a food that suits the body is said to agree with a person.
senses.whyCN: 在健康话题里，适合身体的食物被说成 agree with 某人。

items.cn: 今天它是最常用的表示同意的动词之一。

definition_zh: 这里；在这里；到这里
definition_en: in, at, or to this place or position
core_image: 原地一顿脚：就在这个位置
scene: 导游在路口停下，指着牌子说博物馆就在这里。 Stop here; the museum entrance is just behind that gate.
sceneCN: 这里 here 是「在这个地方」（第 1 个义项：指当前位置）；导游示意就在此处停下。

derivatives.zh: 由 here 加 by 构成，义为「特此；以此」
由 here 加 after 构成，义为「今后；此后」
反义对应词，义为「那里」

senses.title: In or at this place
senses.definition: in or at the place where the speaker is or is pointing
senses.definitionCN: 在说话者所在或所指的地方
senses.example: The keys are here on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙就在这儿桌上。
senses.why: Place words split into near and far; here is the near half, wherever the speaker stands.
senses.whyCN: 地点词分远近，here 指说话者身边的近处。

senses.title: To this place
senses.definition: to this place or position
senses.definitionCN: 朝这个地方来
senses.example: Please bring the chairs here.
senses.exampleCN: 请把椅子搬到这儿来。
senses.why: When movement ends at the speaker, here marks the destination.
senses.whyCN: 当移动以说话者为终点，here 标出目的地。

senses.title: At this point in time or speech
senses.definition: at this point in a text, activity, or process
senses.definitionCN: 在文章、活动或进程的这个节点
senses.example: Here the story takes a surprising turn.
senses.exampleCN: 故事在这里出现惊人转折。
senses.why: Spoken text also has positions; here marks the spot in it.
senses.whyCN: 口头的叙述也有「位置」，here 标出其中的节点。

intro.en: Here is an ancient place adverb, related to he and this.
intro.cn: here 是古老的地点副词，与 he、this 同出一源。

items.en: Old English hēr meant in this place.
items.cn: 古英语 hēr 意为「在这个地方」。

items.en: It goes back to Proto-Germanic *hiar, built on the hi- demonstrative stem.
items.cn: 它源自原始日耳曼语 *hiar，建立在 hi- 指示词干上。

items.en: Middle English kept her, here with the same meaning.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 her、here，意义不变。

items.en: The spelling here became fixed, and compounds like hereby grew.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 here，并派生出 hereby 等复合词。

items.en: Some paired forms such as hither were reinforced by Norse heðan and hither.
items.cn: hither 等成对形式受到古诺斯语 heðan、hither 的强化。

note.en: Here mixes easily with sound-alikes and its opposite.
note.cn: here 易与音近词及反义词混淆。

entries.definition: to receive sound with the ears

entries.definition: a person who inherits property
entries.definitionCN: 「继承人」，美式发音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: in this place; existing here now
entries.definitionCN: 「在场的；本地的」，指当前在场

entries.definition: to this place, old-fashioned
entries.definitionCN: 「到这里」，古旧用法

entries.definition: near or relating to the area around here

normal.cn: here 近、there 远，成对记最稳。

normal.en: hear /hɪə/ and here /hɪə/ sound the same: you hear sounds here.
normal.cn: hear 与 here 同音：你在这里听见声音——一句话锁住两个词。

normal.en: Here you are is said when you hand something over.
normal.cn: 递东西时说 Here you are（给你），场景化记忆。

normal.en: From here on marks a starting point.
normal.cn: from here on（从现在起）把 here 用到时间起点上。

normal.en: Old English hēr still hides inside modern here.
normal.cn: 古英语 hēr 就藏在今天的 here 里，拼写几乎没变。

abstract.en: Stamp your foot once: the spot under your shoe is here.
abstract.cn: 原地跺一下脚：鞋下的那块地方就是 here。

abstract.en: Picture a spotlight fixed on one tile of the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一束聚光灯固定在地板的一块砖上——here 的位置感。

abstract.en: Feel here as a small flag the speaker plants.
abstract.cn: 把 here 感受成说话者插下的一面小旗。

examples.en: Come here and look at this photo of the old bridge.
examples.cn: 过来一下，看看这张老桥的照片。

examples.en: The bus stops here, not at the next corner.
examples.cn: 公共汽车在这里停，不在下一个街角。

examples.en: Here the recipe needs two eggs, not three.
examples.cn: 食谱在这里需要两个鸡蛋，不是三个。

definition_zh: 出生；分娩；诞生；出身
definition_en: the time when a baby comes out of its mother's body, or the beginning of something
core_image: 产房门口的一只小摇篮，旁边放着写有日期的卡片
scene: 医院的走廊上，父亲在登记表上填下孩子出生的日期。 She recorded the date of her son's birth.
sceneCN: 这里 birth 是「出生」（第 1 个义项：婴儿降生这一事实）；句意为她记下了儿子出生的日期。

pos.zh: 名词：出生；分娩；诞生；出身

derivatives.zh: 由 birth 与 day 组合而成，义为「生日」
由 birth 与 place 组合而成，义为「出生地」
由 birth 与 rate 组合而成，义为「出生率」

senses.title: The arrival of a baby
senses.definition: the event in which a baby is born and begins life outside the mother
senses.definitionCN: 婴儿降生、开始在母体外生活这一事件
senses.example: She recorded the date of her son's birth.
senses.exampleCN: 她记下了儿子出生的日期。
senses.why: Old English gebyrd came from the verb beran, to bear or carry, so birth names the moment a child is brought into the world.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gebyrd 来自动词 beran「承载、生育」，所以 birth 指的是孩子被带到世上的那一刻。

senses.title: The act of giving birth
senses.definition: the process by which a woman or an animal gives birth
senses.definitionCN: 女性或动物生下幼崽的过程
senses.example: The birth was long but safe.
senses.exampleCN: 分娩过程很长，但很顺利。
senses.why: Because the same noun covers both the event and the effort behind it, birth can also name the whole process of delivery.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既覆盖事件本身，也覆盖其后的努力，所以 birth 也可以指整个分娩过程。

senses.title: The beginning of something
senses.definition: the time when an idea, an organization, or a country begins
senses.definitionCN: 某个想法、组织或国家开始出现的时间
senses.example: The birth of the internet changed daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 互联网的诞生改变了日常生活。
senses.why: A new idea arrives the way a baby does, suddenly and with a date, so the word for human arrival was borrowed for the start of anything.
senses.whyCN: 新想法到来时就像婴儿降生，有突然性也有日期，于是表示人降生的词被借去指任何事物的开始。

senses.title: Family origin
senses.definition: the social rank or family that a person comes from
senses.definitionCN: 一个人来自的社会等级或家族
senses.example: He is of noble birth.
senses.exampleCN: 他出身贵族。
senses.why: Since family line is fixed at the moment of birth, the word for that moment also came to mean the rank one is born into.
senses.whyCN: 家世在出生的那一刻就定下了，所以表示那一刻的词也引申为「生来所属的等级」。

intro.en: Birth began as a prefixed noun from the verb bear, and the prefix later dropped away.
intro.cn: birth 最初是由动词 bear 加前缀构成的名词，前缀后来脱落了。

items.en: Old English gebyrd came from beran, meaning to bear or to give birth.
items.cn: 古英语 gebyrd 来自 beran，意为「承载、生育」。

items.en: The same verb survives in bear a child and in the related noun burden.
items.cn: 同一个动词仍见于 bear a child，也见于相关名词 burden。

items.en: The old prefix dropped away and the plain form birth became the standard noun.
items.cn: 旧前缀脱落，朴素的 birth 成为标准名词。

items.en: From a person's arrival the word spread to the start of ideas, nations, and organizations.
items.cn: 从人的降生出发，这个词扩展到思想、国家与组织的开端。

items.en: Because family rank is fixed at birth, the word also came to mean social origin.
items.cn: 因为家族等级在出生时就定了，这个词也引申为「社会出身」。

items.en: Today birth covers delivery, origin, and the founding moment of almost anything.
items.cn: 今天 birth 可指分娩、出身，以及几乎任何事物的创立时刻。

normal.cn: birth 来自 bear：give birth 就是「生育孩子」，前缀后来脱落了。

normal.en: Birth, birthday, birthplace and birthrate all keep the same first element.
normal.cn: birth、birthday、birthplace、birthrate 都保留同一个开头成分。

normal.en: A new country or a new idea also has a birth, because both arrive with a date.
normal.cn: 新国家或新想法也有 birth，因为两者都带着一个日期到来。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with give, date of, certificate and rate.
normal.cn: 它常与 give、date of、certificate、rate 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-i-r-t-h; the th at the end is the same ending as in fourth.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-i-r-t-h，末尾的 th 与 fourth 的结尾相同。

abstract.en: See a small cradle outside a hospital room with a date card beside it: that is birth.
abstract.cn: 想象产房外的一只小摇篮，旁边放着写有日期的卡片，那就是 birth。

abstract.en: Put a light bulb in the cradle instead of a baby and the word becomes the start of an idea.
abstract.cn: 把摇篮里的婴儿换成一个灯泡，这个词就变成「想法的开端」。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the cradle bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让摇篮把意思带回来。

examples.en: She recorded the date of her son's birth.
examples.cn: 她记下了儿子出生的日期。

examples.en: The birth of the internet changed daily life.
examples.cn: 互联网的诞生改变了日常生活。

examples.en: He is of noble birth.
examples.cn: 他出身贵族。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必死」——古时生育风险高，母亲和孩子都拼命：出生

root: birth 来自古英语 gebyrd，由动词 beran「承载、生育」加前缀构成，后来前缀脱落成为 birth。它先指婴儿降生，再扩展到分娩过程；因为新事物也像婴儿一样带着日期到来，于是有了「诞生」义；又因为家世在出生那一刻就定下，于是有了「出身」义。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of birth come from one moment: a new life arriving, and everything fixed or begun at that moment.
sensesIntro.cn: birth 的四个义项都出自同一个时刻：新生命到来，以及在这一刻被定下或开启的一切。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cradle outside a hospital room with a date card
core.cn: 核心意象：产房外的一只摇篮和一张写有日期的卡片

branches.en: THE ARRIVAL: the first sense is the baby coming into the world.
branches.cn: 降生线：第一个义项就是婴儿来到世上。

branches.en: THE EFFORT: the same noun covers the delivery that makes the arrival happen.
branches.cn: 分娩线：同一个名词也覆盖促成降生的分娩过程。

branches.en: THE START: ideas and nations arrive with a date, so they also have a birth.
branches.cn: 开端线：思想与国家也带着日期到来，所以它们也有 birth。

branches.en: THE RANK: the family one is born into fixes one's social origin.
branches.cn: 等级线：出生的家族决定了一个人的社会出身。

branches.en: THE SAME SHAPE: a baby and a new idea both begin at one marked moment.
branches.cn: 同一形状：婴儿与新想法都在某个被标记的时刻开始。

intro.en: Birth is a derived noun; the items below are its old prefix, its root verb, and the compounds built on it.
intro.cn: birth 是派生名词，下面列出的是它的旧前缀、词根动词以及由它构成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nativitas and parere are recorded words for birth and to give birth; they are parallels, not sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nativitas 与 parere 分别表示「出生」与「生育」，此处作为平行词列出，而非来源。

items.example: It appears in the older form gebyrd.
She will bear a child in spring.

items.meaning: the act or time of being born
items.example: The birth took place at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 孩子是在黎明时出生的。

items.example: It forms birth from the root of bear.
items.exampleCN: 它由 bear 的词根构成 birth。

definition_zh: 更少的；较少的；减去；不及
definition_en: a smaller amount or degree; to a smaller extent; minus a quantity
core_image: 同样一只杯子，水面比上次低了一截
scene: 期末比期中少睡了许多，他的黑眼圈更深了。 This year we have less snow than last year.
sceneCN: 这里 less 是「量或程度的较小」（第 1 个义项：更少的）；句意为今年雪比去年少。

derivatives.zh: less 加后缀 -er，指「较小的；次要的」
less 的最高级，指「最小的；最少的」
less 加动词后缀 -en，指「减少；削弱」

senses.title: A smaller amount
senses.definition: a smaller amount or degree of something
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度上更小的
senses.example: This year we have less snow than last year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年雪比去年少。
senses.why: Little steps down to less: the same smallness, now compared.
senses.whyCN: little 的比较级就是 less：同一种「小」，只是加上了比较。

senses.title: To a smaller extent
senses.definition: to a smaller degree; not so much
senses.definitionCN: 程度上较小；没那么……
senses.example: The second film was less exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 第二部电影没那么刺激。
senses.why: Degree shrinks the same way amount does, so the adverb follows the determiner.
senses.whyCN: 程度与数量同样收缩，副词于是跟随限定词。

senses.title: Minus a quantity
senses.definition: after taking away a stated amount
senses.definitionCN: 扣除一定数额之后
senses.example: Nine hundred dollars less tax.
senses.exampleCN: 九百美元扣税后。
senses.why: Taking away shrinks the pile, matching the image of a smaller amount.
senses.whyCN: 扣除使总量变小，与「更少」意象吻合。

senses.title: Not as important or worthy
senses.definition: used to say something is lower in rank or importance
senses.definitionCN: 表示级别或重要性更低
senses.example: Try not to think of it as a lesser task.
senses.exampleCN: 尽量别把它当作次要任务。
senses.why: Being smaller in amount becomes being smaller in worth.
senses.whyCN: 数量之小延伸为价值之低。

senses.title: Even less or none at all
senses.definition: used to intensify a negative, as in still less
senses.definitionCN: 加强否定，如 still less
senses.example: He hardly reads, still less writes.
senses.exampleCN: 他几乎不读书，更别提写作了。
senses.why: If the small thing fails, the smaller one fails more, so less sharpens the negative.
senses.whyCN: 小的尚且不行，更小的更不行，less 因此加强否定。

senses.title: No less — surprisingly much
senses.definition: used to show that an amount is surprisingly large
senses.definitionCN: 表示数量大得出人意料
senses.example: No less than fifty students joined.
senses.exampleCN: 多达五十名学生参加。
senses.why: Doubling the negative form flips the feeling: less phrases can mean much.
senses.whyCN: 否定形式反转出情感：less 的短语也能表示「多」。

intro.en: Less is the comparative of little, from Old English laes, of Germanic origin; its exact root beyond Germanic is uncertain.
intro.cn: less 是 little 的比较级，来自古英语 laes，属日耳曼语源；日耳曼语之外的词根不确定。

items.en: Old English laes was the comparative of lyt 'little', meaning 'smaller, fewer'.
items.cn: 古英语 laes 是 lyt「小」的比较级，意为「更小、更少」。

items.en: Germanic *laisizan underlies the form; related little kept a diminutive ending.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 *laisizan 是其基础；little 则保留了指小词尾。

items.en: Middle English spread less to abstract degree and arithmetic subtraction.
items.cn: 中古英语把 less 扩展到抽象程度与算术减法。

items.en: Modern English fixed less for uncountable amounts, in contrast to fewer.
items.cn: 现代英语固定 less 用于不可数量，与 fewer 相对。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Germanic trail of the little-family is not agreed on.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：little 词族在日耳曼语之前的轨迹尚无定论。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes; group two collects the amount-comparing family.
note.cn: 第一组区分形近词；第二组收集比较数量的词族。

entries.definition: A class or task; shares five letters but a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 课程；共享五个字母，词根不同。

entries.definition: The adjective form of less for rank and importance.
entries.definitionCN: less 的形容词形式，指级别与重要性。

entries.definition: The superlative of little and less.
entries.definitionCN: little 与 less 的最高级。

entries.definition: For countable things; less is for amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 用于可数；less 用于不可数量。

entries.definition: The arithmetic word for taking away.
entries.definitionCN: 算术中的「减去」。

entries.definition: Smaller in degree or position.
entries.definitionCN: 程度或位置更低。

entries.definition: The base adjective; less is its comparative.
entries.definitionCN: 原级形容词；less 是其比较级。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the little-family and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用 little 词族与固定搭配。

normal.en: Less is the comparative of little; least is the superlative.
normal.cn: less 是 little 的比较级；least 是最高级。

normal.en: Use less for amounts, fewer for counts: less water, fewer bottles.
normal.cn: 量用 less，可数用 fewer：less water、fewer bottles。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: no less than, more or less, none the less.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：多达、或多或少、尽管如此。

normal.en: Lessen is the verb: to make less.
normal.cn: lessen 是动词：使更少。

normal.en: Nine dollars less tax means after tax is taken away.
normal.cn: nine dollars less tax 指扣税之后。

abstract.en: Picture one glass with a visibly lower water line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子水位明显更低。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt where tax is sliced off the total.
abstract.cn: 想象账单上税额从总额里被切掉。

abstract.en: Picture a shrinking row of books, one less each week.
abstract.cn: 想象一排书逐周减少，一本更比一本少。

examples.en: There is less traffic on Sundays.
examples.cn: 周日路上车少。

examples.en: The trip took two hours less than we expected.
examples.cn: 旅程比预期少花两小时。

examples.en: She earns less but enjoys the work more.
examples.cn: 她挣得更少，却更喜欢这份工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累死」——钱越挣越少，累死了 → 更少

root: 古英语 laes「较小」，日耳曼语源，是 little 的比较级；更早词根不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses compare downward: smaller amounts, smaller degrees, subtraction, lower worth, sharpened negatives, and a flipped phrase meaning much.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项一路向下比：更小的量、更低的程度、减法、更低的价值、强化的否定，以及反转出「多达」的短语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the water line drops; the same container holds less.
core.cn: 核心意象：水位下降，同一容器装得更少。

branches.en: SMALLER EVERYWHERE: amounts and degrees shrink together.
branches.cn: 处处变小：数量与程度一同收缩。

branches.en: TAKING AWAY: subtraction is less written as arithmetic.
branches.cn: 减去：减法就是 less 的算术形态。

branches.en: SMALL IN WORTH: little amount becomes low rank.
branches.cn: 价值之小：数量小变成级别低。

branches.en: SHARPENED NEGATIVES: still less pushes denial further.
branches.cn: 强化否定：still less 把否定推得更远。

branches.en: THE FLIP SIDE: no less than surprisingly means much.
branches.cn: 反转面：no less than 出人意料地表示多。

intro.en: Less is a short native comparative with no prefixes; its family is little, least, lesser and lessen.
intro.cn: less 是无前缀的本族比较级；词族为 little、least、lesser、lessen。

latinIntro.en: No established Latin cognate exists, so the Latin section stays empty; the items show the native family.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目展示本族词族。

items.example: A lesser poet still wrote well.

items.exampleCN: 它把 less 变成 lessen。

items.example: The work is more or less done.

最小的
减少

definition_zh: 在……之中；在……中间；其中之一
definition_en: in the middle of a group, or surrounded by things, or one of a number
core_image: 一群学生中间站着新来的同学
scene: 一群学生中间站着一位新来的同学。 A new pupil stood among the students.
sceneCN: 这里 among 是「在……之中」（第 1 个义项：处在群体内部）；句意为一位新同学站在学生们中间。

pos.zh: 介词：在……之中；在……中间；其中之一

derivatives.zh: 在……之中（英式变体）
在……之中
在两者之间

senses.title: Inside a group of people
senses.definition: in the middle of a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 处在一群人的中间
senses.example: A new pupil stood among the students.
senses.exampleCN: 一位新同学站在学生们中间。
senses.why: The old word meant in the crowd, so being inside a group is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古词意为「在人群中」，所以处在群体内部是第一义。

senses.title: Surrounded by things
senses.definition: surrounded by things on all sides
senses.definitionCN: 四周都被事物围住
senses.example: A small house stands among the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 一座小房子坐落在树丛中。
senses.why: The crowd was replaced by objects, and being inside a crowd became being surrounded by things.
senses.whyCN: 人群换成物体，「在人群里」就变成四周被事物包围。

senses.title: One of a number
senses.definition: included in a set as one member
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个成员被包含在一组里
senses.example: He is one among many young writers.
senses.exampleCN: 他是众多年轻作家中的一位。
senses.why: The same inside position marks a member counted with the rest, which gives the sense of one of a number.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「在里面」的位置标记被数在其中的成员，这就是其中之一。

intro.en: The recorded history of among is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 among 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: The old phrase meant in a crowd or in a mingling.
items.cn: 古短语意为在人群中，或处在混杂之中。

items.en: Middle English shortened it to among.
items.cn: 中古英语把它缩短为 among。

items.en: English used among for being inside a group.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 among 指处在群体内部。

items.en: Later it covered being surrounded by things as well as people.
items.cn: 后来它也覆盖被事物包围的情形。

items.en: Today it also marks one member of a set.
items.cn: 今天它也标记一组中的一个成员。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The British variant with the same meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 英式变体，意思相同。

entries.definition: It looks close but means a quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 外观相近，但指数量。

entries.definition: It also means in the middle of.
entries.definitionCN: 也表示在……之中。

entries.definition: It is common before events or surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 常用于事件或环境之前。

entries.definition: It points to two sides rather than a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指向两边，而非一个群体。

entries.definition: It stresses being inside limits.
entries.definitionCN: 强调在界限之内。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The old word meant in the crowd: among is being inside a group, not outside it.
normal.cn: 古词意为「在人群中」：among 就是处在群体内部，而不是外面。

normal.en: The same family also gives amongst and amid.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 amongst 与 amid。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase among the trees.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「在树丛中」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of among in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 among 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: in the middle of a group, or surrounded by things, or one of a number.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「在……之中」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a new pupil standing inside a group of students.
abstract.cn: 想象一群学生中间站着新来的同学。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: A new pupil stood among the students.
examples.cn: 一位新同学站在学生们中间。

examples.en: A small house stands among the trees.
examples.cn: 一座小房子坐落在树丛中。

examples.en: He is one among many young writers.
examples.cn: 他是众多年轻作家中的一位。

root: among 来自古英语短语 on gemang「在人群之中」；中古英语缩短为 among，十四世纪指处在群体内部，后来也指被事物包围，今天还可标记一组中的一个成员。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of among grows from one core image: a new pupil standing inside a group of students.
sensesIntro.cn: among 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：一群学生中间站着新来的同学。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new pupil standing inside a group of students
core.cn: 核心意象：一群学生中间站着新来的同学

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: Inside a group of people.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：处在人群之中。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: Surrounded by things.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：被事物包围。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: Inside a group of people / Surrounded by things.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：处在人群之中、被事物包围。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: One of a number.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：其中之一。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 03 covers the outer edge of the meaning: Inside a group of people / One of a number.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖意义的边缘：处在人群之中、其中之一。

intro.en: among can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: among 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.example: It comes from the old phrase on gemang.
items.exampleCN: 它来自古短语 on gemang。

items.example: It gives the picture of being in a crowd.
items.exampleCN: 它给出处在人群中的画面。

items.example: It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.
It names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

items.example: It turns an adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表状态的名词。

definition_zh: 危险；险境；危险的人或物
definition_en: the possibility that someone or something will be harmed
core_image: 深潭边缘那块摇摇晃晃的湿石头
scene: 游泳课结束前，教练站在池边举起红色提示牌。 The coach reminded us that the deep end of the pool is a danger for beginners.
sceneCN: 这里 danger 是「危险」（第 1 个义项：可能受到伤害的状况）；句意是教练提醒我们泳池深水区对初学者来说有危险。

derivatives.zh: 由 danger 加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，义为「危险的」
由动词前缀 en- 加 danger 构成，义为「危及；使遭受危险」

senses.title: The chance of being hurt
senses.definition: the possibility that harm, injury or loss will happen
senses.definitionCN: 伤害、损失可能发生的状态
senses.example: Cyclists should know that riding without a helmet is a danger.
senses.exampleCN: 骑自行车的人应该明白，不戴头盔骑行是危险的。
senses.why: A narrow slippery ledge holds you above harm, so the place itself feels like the possibility of harm.
senses.whyCN: 又窄又滑的岩沿悬在伤害之上，那个位置本身就让人感到危险的可能。

senses.title: A person or thing that can cause harm
senses.definition: a person, animal or thing that may cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害的人、动物或事物
senses.example: The broken swing in the playground is a danger to small children.
senses.exampleCN: 游乐场里坏掉的秋千对小孩子是个危险物。
senses.why: When the source of the possibility can be pointed at, the pointer gets the name.
senses.whyCN: 当危险的可能性能被指认出源头，源头便获得了这个名字。

intro.en: Danger once meant the power of a lord over your fate.
intro.cn: danger 最初的意思是「领主对你命运的支配权」。

items.en: dominium meant lordly power or ownership, from dominus, a lord or master.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dominium 意为主人的权力或所有权，来自 dominus（主人）。

items.en: Old French dangier meant power to harm, the authority of a lord.
items.cn: 古法语 dangier 意为伤害之权，即领主的威权。

items.en: English took danger in the twelfth century with that sense of lordly power over someone.
items.cn: 英语在十二世纪吸收 danger，仍指对人的支配权。

items.en: Because a lord's whim could hurt you, the word slid to mean risk of harm itself.
items.cn: 因为领主的兴致可能带来伤害，这个词滑向「受伤的风险」本身。

items.en: Today danger names warnings, risk and anything harmful, from signs to storms.
items.cn: 如今 danger 指警示、风险和一切有害之物，从警示牌到风暴。

note.en: These words share the Latin root dominus or describe harm and risk.
note.cn: 这些词与拉丁词根 dominus 同源，或描述伤害与风险。

definition_zh: 许诺；答应；承诺；诺言；希望；前途
definition_en: to say firmly that one will do something, the statement so made, and the signs that something good is likely to come
core_image: 两只手伸出去一击为定，把一句还看不见的话变成双方都得守住的东西
scene: 临行前，父亲把旧钥匙放进儿子手里，说定秋天一定回来看那棵老树。 Before he left, he promised to come back for the harvest.
sceneCN: 这里表示「许诺、答应」（第 1 个义项：明确说出自己一定会做某事）；句意为他在离开之前答应回来参加秋收。

derivatives.zh: 由 promise 加 -ing 构成，义为「有前途的；有希望的」
由拉丁词干 promiss- 加 -ory 构成，义为「承诺的；约定的」，常见于法律文书
由 promising 再加 -ly 构成，义为「有希望地；看来不错地」

senses.title: To say firmly that one will do something
senses.definition: to tell someone that you will certainly do something, so that the other person can count on it
senses.definitionCN: 明确告诉某人自己一定会做某事，使对方可以指望
senses.example: She promised to call as soon as she landed.
senses.exampleCN: 她答应一下飞机就打电话。
senses.why: The Latin verb sent a word forward toward the listener, so the act begins as a message travelling out of the speaker's mouth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词的意思是「把话往前送」，所以这个动作起初是一句话从说话人嘴里飞向听者。

senses.title: A statement that one will certainly do something
senses.definition: a statement in which someone says that they will certainly do something
senses.definitionCN: 某人说定自己一定会做某事的说法
senses.example: He kept every promise he made that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那个夏天他许下的每个诺言都守住了。
senses.why: Once spoken, the message no longer belongs to the speaker alone; it can be kept, quoted or thrown back, which is how the verb turns into the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 话一出口就不再只属于说话人，它会被收着、被引用、被拿出来对质；动词就这样变成了那个被送出的东西。

senses.title: To show signs that something good is likely
senses.definition: to give signs that something good or important is likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 显出好结果或重要事情很可能发生的迹象
senses.example: The early sales figures promise a strong year.
senses.exampleCN: 早期销售数字预示着这一年会很不错。
senses.why: A pledge always leans toward a future that has not arrived; when clouds or numbers do the leaning, the word keeps only that forward look and drops the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 诺言本就朝着一个还没到来的将来倾斜；当乌云或数字在倾斜时，这个词只留下「朝前指」的动作，说话人则退场了。

senses.title: The quality of seeming likely to succeed
senses.definition: the quality of seeming likely to succeed, especially in a young person or a new project
senses.definitionCN: 看起来很可能成功的那份质地，尤指年轻人或新项目身上的
senses.example: The young pianist showed promise from her first recital.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻钢琴家从第一场独奏会起就显出前途。
senses.why: If the good thing is promised but has not arrived, the noun can name that waiting good thing directly, and English does so especially for talent that has not yet proved itself.
senses.whyCN: 如果好事已被许诺却还没到，名词就能直接指那件正在等着的好事；英语尤其用它来说尚未证明自己的才华。

intro.en: Promise comes from a Latin verb meaning to send a word forward, and the English word still has the shape of a message flying toward someone who will hold you to it.
intro.cn: promise 来自一个意为「把话往前送」的拉丁动词，这个词至今保持着「一句话飞向对方，对方据此要求你兑现」的形状。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go, and it sits inside many English words about sending and releasing.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放走，是许多表示「送出、释放」的英语词里的那个成分。

items.en: The prefix pro- pushed the sending forward, so promittere meant to send a word forth, that is, to give someone your word.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 把「送」推向前面，于是 promittere 意为把话送出去，也就是向人许下诺言。

items.en: The participle promissum named the thing sent forth rather than the sending, and it is the direct source of the noun.
items.cn: 分词 promissum 指被送出的那个东西，而不是送的动作，是名词义项的直接来源。

items.en: Old French kept the noun as promesse, meaning a pledge, and English borrowed it with the ending reshaped as promise.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词写作 promesse，意为诺言，英语借入时把词尾改成 promise。

items.en: English uses the verb for giving one's word and the noun for the word given, then stretches both to the hopeful signs that point at a good future.
items.cn: 现代英语用动词指给出承诺，用名词指给出的那句话，再把两者扩展到指向美好未来的种种迹象。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of sending, including a legal pair for the two sides of a pledge; the second group gathers words for solemn promises.
note.cn: 第一组共用表示「送出」的拉丁动词，还包括指承诺双方的一对法律用语；第二组收表示郑重许诺的词。

entries.definition: Relating to a promise, especially one that has legal force.
entries.definitionCN: 与承诺有关的，尤指具有法律效力的承诺。

entries.definition: In law, the person to whom a promise is made.
entries.definitionCN: 法律用语，指接受承诺的一方。

entries.definition: In law, the person who makes a promise.
entries.definitionCN: 法律用语，指做出承诺的一方。

entries.definition: A statement assumed true as a basis for reasoning; it shares the Latin verb of sending but not the sense of pledging.
entries.definitionCN: 推理时被当作前提的陈述；与本词共用拉丁「送」动词，但没有许诺之义。

entries.definition: A serious promise, often backed by something given as security.
entries.definitionCN: 郑重的承诺，常以某物作担保。

entries.definition: A solemn promise, especially one about marriage or faith.
entries.definitionCN: 庄严的誓愿，尤指关于婚姻或信仰的。

entries.definition: A formal promise made before a witness or on something sacred.
entries.definitionCN: 在见证人面前或对神圣之物做出的正式承诺。

entries.definition: A statement meant to give someone confidence about the future.
entries.definitionCN: 意在让人对将来安心的说法。

normalIntro.en: Every sense keeps the picture of a word sent forward: someone speaks, the word travels, and the listener is then entitled to expect something.
normalIntro.cn: 每个义项都保留着「一句话被送出去」的画面：有人开口，话飞过去，听的人从此有权期待某件事。

normal.en: Mittere is Latin for to send, and pro- pushes it forward, so promittere is to send a word ahead of you.
normal.cn: mittere 是拉丁语的「送」，pro- 把它往前推，所以 promittere 就是「把话先送出去」。

normal.en: Promissum is the thing that was sent, which is why the noun means the word given and not the act of giving it.
normal.cn: promissum 是被送出的那个东西，所以名词义指说出的那句话，而不是说这句话的动作。

normal.en: Promising adds -ing to describe someone or something that already looks like a coming success.
normal.cn: promising 加 -ing，用来形容已经显出成功样子的年轻人或事物。

normal.en: Weather that promises rain keeps only the forward-pointing part of a pledge, with nobody actually pledging.
normal.cn: 天气 promise rain 只保留了许诺中「朝前指」的那一半，并没有谁真的在许诺。

normal.en: Keep and break fit promise because a pledge is treated like an object held in the hand or dropped on the floor.
normal.cn: keep 与 break 能配 promise，是因为诺言被当成手里的东西：可以握住，也可以摔掉。

abstract.en: A promise is a word lent forward in time, and the debt is settled when that future finally arrives.
abstract.cn: 诺言是一句被借到将来的话，等那个将来真的到来，债才算还清。

abstract.en: One word covers a pledge and a hopeful sign because both are the present pointing at something not yet here.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指誓言，也指好兆头，因为两者都是「现在」在指向尚未到来的东西。

abstract.en: To promise is to make your future self answerable to another person's memory of what you said.
abstract.cn: 许诺就是让你的将来那个自己去面对别人记住的那句话。

examples.en: She promised to send the file before noon.
examples.cn: 她答应中午前把文件发过去。

examples.en: He broke his promise and never mentioned it again.
examples.cn: 他违背了诺言，此后再没提起。

examples.en: The new treatment promises to help patients who failed older drugs.
examples.cn: 这种新疗法有望帮助那些对旧药无效的病人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若米事」——说出口的事像米粒撒出去，收不回来，只能认账；记住 promise 是许诺。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ mittere（送、放出）→ promittere（把话送出去、许下诺言）→ promissum（被送出的承诺），经古法语 promesse 进入英语；同族词多与「送出、放出」有关，premise 与本词共用 mittere，但前缀不同、意义也走远。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a word sent forward to bind the speaker; from it come the pledge itself, the hopeful sign, and the promise that a future holds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「一句被送出去、用来约束说话人的话」；由此分出那句诺言本身、指向好结果的迹象，以及关于前途的希望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands meeting in a hard clasp, turning spoken words into something both sides must keep.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手用力一击，把说出口的话变成双方都得守住的东西。

branches.en: a hand stretched out before the sentence is finished
branches.cn: 话还没说完，手已经伸了出去

branches.en: a written pledge folded away in a drawer
branches.cn: 写下来的承诺折好收进抽屉

branches.en: dark clouds carrying the smell of coming rain
branches.cn: 带着雨意的乌云压在天边

branches.en: a young musician whose future seems already waiting
branches.cn: 前途仿佛已经在前方等着的年轻乐手

branches.en: one word for a vow and for a hope
branches.cn: 同一个词既指誓言，也指希望

intro.en: A Latin verb of sending, its forward prefix, and the endings that turn the message into a noun and an adjective hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「送」的拉丁动词、表示向前的前缀，以及把这句话变成名词与形容词的词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb promittere and its participle promissum are the reliable cognates behind the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 promittere 及其分词 promissum，是英语这个词可靠的同源词。
